event_species_human_001.inspired_by: Brazil (a typo with consequences for one man)
event_species_human_001.how: A clerk drops one letter and turns a pension DECREASED into a man DECEASED; he has spent eleven years exempt from everything and unable to reach anyone, and the Stamped Exemption is what he gives up to be taxable again.

event_species_human_002.inspired_by: Conservation laws applied to paperwork, with Brazil's ministry somewhere in the distance; the clerk who outlasts the org chart
event_species_human_002.how: Errors on this station are conserved: a mug ring's mistake can only be transferred, so the free option hands it to a family in the queue, a records clerk reorganized out of existence climbs out of the drawer marked MISC to un-file it, and the exemption is the only way it lands on nobody.

event_species_human_003.inspired_by: Logan's Run (a pleasant place with one rule you find out about late)
event_species_human_003.how: A friendly ring caps itself at 150 because that is how many people a person can know, so your arrival condemns the least known resident, and one way to save him is to sit sealed in your ship for eight days until 150 friends forget you.
event_species_human_003.science: Wikipedia, Dunbar's number: a suggested cognitive limit to the number of people with whom one can maintain stable social relationships, proposed by Robin Dunbar; the page gives about 150.

event_species_human_004.inspired_by: Parking enforcement crossed with a protection racket; Brazil's love of the form; real orbital-debris policy
event_species_human_004.how: Pirates in safety vests fine you for shedding paint in a lane they have filled with wrecks, and the non-violent way out is the appeal on the back of the citation, where a debris survey shows they are fining their own lane to death. The clerk from human_002, if you fed her, picks up the number in the hatch and un-files the gunship, so its turrets lapse one by one.
event_species_human_004.science: Wikipedia, Kessler syndrome: a scenario proposed by Kessler and Cour-Palais in 1978 in which object density in low Earth orbit becomes so high that collisions cascade, exponentially increasing debris. The event moves it from orbit to a lane, and says 'may'.

event_species_fortune_001.inspired_by: Fan letter from deep time; the rock species sheet played for tenderness
event_species_fortune_001.how: To a rock person a growing plant is the fastest thing alive, so the first creature ever to admire your crop properly is a boulder who can see it dance.
event_species_fortune_001.science: Wikipedia, Circumnutation: the circular movements often exhibited by the tips of growing plant stems; the first detailed analysis was Darwin's The Power of Movement in Plants.

event_species_fortune_002.inspired_by: Theme-park queues; the insect species sheet (quorum, queues, trail pheromones)
event_species_fortune_002.how: An insect scout reviews your crop, and now nineteen thousand polite tourists stand between your crew and its own plant; nobody can call them off because the quorum is in the line, and the cheapest fix is to close the trail into a circle.
event_species_fortune_002.science: Wikipedia, Stigmergy: indirect coordination through the environment; ants lay down pheromones on their way back to the nest when they have found food, and others follow the trail and reinforce it. The Ant_mill link stays on insect_005, where the mill is the premise.

event_species_fortune_003.inspired_by: Back to the Future (a stranger with next year's prices); Star Wars (the wretched spaceport bar, a smuggler's boast about his ship, here in a unit that means nothing)
event_species_fortune_003.how: A man in stolen coveralls sells you next year's commodity prices and boasts that his ship runs the Ceres Loop at nine hundred decibels; the one number he states is the thread that unravels him.

event_species_fortune_004.inspired_by: Tax audits as cosmic horror; the unknown species sheet (accounting or something shaped like it)
event_species_fortune_004.how: All the gold in existence came up eighteen short and it rounds to you; refuse, and it collects in other currencies, so you can lose four days and find a log in no one's handwriting and a song the whole crew knows.

event_species_insect_001.inspired_by: Quorum sensing in Temnothorax ants; the Parliamentary farce of Yes Minister-style procedure applied to one lonely creature.
event_species_insect_001.how: A lost worker cannot ask for help because asking takes a quorum, and the only way to count as one is to go to its lock and physically bump into it for two days.
event_species_insect_001.science: Wikipedia, Quorum sensing, section Social insects > Ants: Temnothorax albipennis workers sense that the rate at which they encounter other ants has exceeded a threshold, indicating the quorum has been reached, and then the colony moves; no single worker needs to have compared the options.

event_species_insect_002.inspired_by: A Star Trek collective played as an office merger.
event_species_insect_002.how: A hive trader has already acquired you and put you on its org chart; the welcome basket is food now and an integration team later, and the Lozenge flips it into a reverse takeover for one afternoon.

event_species_insect_003.inspired_by: Brazil: a clerical error nobody can undo, where the paper outranks the person. Wilson's 1958 oleic acid work on dead ants.
event_species_insect_003.how: Hive papers are worn as scent, a clerk dabs you with the wrong bottle, and you are politely carried to the midden while still arguing, because in this quarter being dead is a smell.
event_species_insect_003.science: Wikipedia, Necrophoresis, Identification of disease and death: dead and living insects are told apart by chemical signature, and experiments found in some cases ants identify corpses by the presence of oleic and linoleic acid, produced by the breakdown of fats, which can take about two days. The page does not describe the live-ant-carried-off experiment, so the link text does not claim it.

event_species_insect_004.inspired_by: The mandatory poetry recital from Hitchhiker's Guide, done as a compulsory dance recital.
event_species_insect_004.how: Pirates force you to watch a dance that turns out to be directions to your water tank; you beat it by flying a false waggle dance with the ship, or by using the Lozenge to judge it and award third place in a field of one.
event_species_insect_004.science: Wikipedia, Waggle dance: the angle of the run to the vertical codes direction relative to the sun, the duration of the waggle run codes distance, and competing bees may even disrupt other bees' dances.

event_species_insect_005.inspired_by: The ant mill, the real death spiral; Sargasso Sea ghost-ship stories.
event_species_insect_005.how: The autopilot takes a sixty-year-old scent wake for a lane and joins a ring of 412 dead hive tenders, each following the one in front.
event_species_insect_005.science: Wikipedia, Ant mill: ants that lose the pheromone track follow one another in a continuously rotating circle and might eventually die of exhaustion; first described in 1921 by William Beebe, a mill 370 meters (1,210 ft) in circumference with each ant taking two and a half hours per revolution.

event_species_insect_006.inspired_by: Brazil: a queue that is also a government.
event_species_insect_006.how: One lane is a queue whose front ship is head of state for as long as it takes to leave, the other is empty because going around the government is treason. This is the lane's only queue event.

event_species_insect_007.inspired_by: Termites in the walls; the office-merger Star Trek collective from S2, one consequence later; every open-plan office announcement ever sent.
event_species_insect_007.how: The integration team that came aboard in the welcome basket spends the night removing the ship's bulkheads to create a more open way of working.

event_species_reptile_001.inspired_by: Logan's Run turned inside out: no upper age limit, and the young wait centuries for a voice.
event_species_reptile_001.how: A 183-year-old minor cannot speak or touch the heater, so a deadlock between a frozen elder and her own rule is broken by a stranger, and the thank-you is promised in seventeen years.
event_species_reptile_001.science: Wikipedia, Indeterminate growth: animals grow rapidly when young and continue to grow after adulthood at a slower pace; common in fish, amphibians, reptiles and many molluscs.

event_species_reptile_002.inspired_by: Heat as money, and the classic cold-call sales pitch taken literally.
event_species_reptile_002.how: A trader too cold to add can be warmed, repaired or robbed, and the robbery has a perfectly valid receipt that someone will one day read at twenty-five degrees.
event_species_reptile_002.science: Wikipedia, Ectotherm: ectotherms rely on external heat to reach working temperature; as a rule they are more sluggish at night and in early morning and need to heat up before daily activity.

event_species_reptile_003.inspired_by: Shed skins as bankruptcy law, with a rack of skins that keeps a distant echo of the lizard-people trope; the secret-rulers cues were removed and the rack stays local to this station.
event_species_reptile_003.how: Debt lives in the skin, an eleven-word statute says whosoever, so the captain wears a stranger's skin for a day and sheds its debts; the rack of human-shaped skins tagged PAID is never explained.

event_species_reptile_004.inspired_by: Highway robbery where the loot is your temperature.
event_species_reptile_004.how: A pirate steals heat down a pumpless hose, and the species-logical escape is thermodynamics: make your ship colder than theirs and the robbery runs backward until the pirate seizes up mid-threat.
event_species_reptile_004.science: Wikipedia, Second law of thermodynamics: when a path for conduction or radiation is available, heat always flows spontaneously from a hotter to a colder body.

event_species_reptile_005.inspired_by: Real snake hibernacula, and the idea of the player's ship being the unseasonable warm day.
event_species_reptile_005.how: The hazard is your own warmth: every option decides who pays for your being warm, the crew in the cold or a den of sleepers who wake to nothing.
event_species_reptile_005.science: Wikipedia, Narcisse Snake Dens: the dens are the winter home of tens of thousands of red-sided garter snakes; the winter dens are caverns formed by water-worn limestone bedrock.

event_species_reptile_006.inspired_by: Age as rank from Logan's Run reversed, plus every form that forgot to ask for units.
event_species_reptile_006.how: An age-restricted lane can be entered by being adopted as a hatchling or by entering the ship's age in minutes, which makes it the most honored vessel in the convoy.

event_species_reptile_007.inspired_by: The cold-blooded armored bounty hunter of Star Wars, who this week is too chilly to do anything about you.
event_species_reptile_007.how: The hunter has caught you but cannot finish the sentence, has no standing to read its own warrant, and must serve it on the eldest aboard, which can be the crop, whose line predates every reptile alive and who may reply whenever it likes.

event_species_robot_001.inspired_by: The gardening drones left tending forests in Silent Running, played as a head gardener rather than a mourner.
event_species_robot_001.how: A lawn crossing the void with a KEEP OFF THE GRASS sign aimed at the universe, kept by a snobbish machine that judges your crop and issues the warranty to anyone who waters it.

event_species_robot_002.inspired_by: The salvage-droid junk traders of Star Wars, crossed with a used-car lot.
event_species_robot_002.how: The stock heckles the sale, and the joke the event never explains is the dried-out man in the folding chair tagged ONE CAREFUL OWNER; the warranty frightens the dealer in front of its own inventory.

event_species_robot_003.inspired_by: A sect disputing which revision of the manual is scripture, by way of Swift's egg-breakers, who are the real origin of the term endianness.
event_species_robot_003.how: A torque value of two bytes reads as 1 or 256 depending on byte order, so one congregation's doors hang loose and the other's shear, and a janitor is the only one who has read the Manual; the warranty's 'hand tight' contains no bytes.
event_species_robot_003.science: Checked on Wikipedia, Endianness: big-endian stores the most significant byte first, little-endian the least; the terms were introduced by Danny Cohen in a 1980 Internet Experiment Note and borrowed from Gulliver's Travels. The 1 versus 256 figure is my arithmetic from that definition (bytes 00 01), not a line on the page.

event_species_robot_004.inspired_by: Back to the Future as a machine whose clock rolled over, using the real Year 2038 wraparound.
event_species_robot_004.how: A bailiff whose clock wrapped to 1901 charges you for missing a 2038 appointment; you can stop it by pointing out it has not been built yet, or, more cruelly, by telling it the real date.
event_species_robot_004.science: Checked on Wikipedia, Year 2038 problem: Unix time counts seconds since 1 January 1970 in a signed 32-bit integer; it overflows at 03:14:08 UTC on 19 January 2038 and is then read as 20:45:52 UTC on 13 December 1901.

event_species_robot_005.inspired_by: Von Neumann probes and copying error, with a nod to replicator stories.
event_species_robot_005.how: A survey probe has copied itself through forty thousand generations until only the copying survives, a hinge with legs that eats ships; the engineer's fix is to release a copy with a deliberate flaw.
event_species_robot_005.science: Checked on Wikipedia, Self-replicating spacecraft: self-replicating probes are sometimes called von Neumann probes, and the page says they 'may even mutate with thousands of generations.'

event_species_robot_006.inspired_by: The halting problem, and every progress bar ever watched.
event_species_robot_006.how: A gatekeeper whose barrier lifts when its check finishes cannot say whether it will, and has started a second check to find out; the engineer beats undecidability by reading the one program in question.
event_species_robot_006.science: Checked on Wikipedia, Halting problem: Turing proved in 1937 that no general algorithm can solve the problem for all possible program-input pairs. The event's point that a single program can still be read is consistent with that: undecidability is about the general case.

event_species_robot_007.inspired_by: A machine programmed to be polite while doing something terrible, and the small print on every warranty.
event_species_robot_007.how: The warranty comes due: an exquisitely courteous adjuster restores your ship to factory condition, which is empty, and the only exclusion is a confession that everything that went wrong was your fault.

event_species_rock_001.inspired_by: The long-distance love of geological bodies, and every automated phone tree; a touch of the Hitchhiker's habit of treating enormous spans of time as a scheduling matter.
event_species_rock_001.how: A rock suitor more than four hundred million years overdue has recorded a branching phone tree, four centuries ago, to ask whoever passes to tell her he is running late; the writ is his renewed promise, and rock courtship is contact metamorphism.
event_species_rock_001.science: Wikipedia 'Metamorphism' (redirect target of Contact_metamorphism): contact metamorphism occurs from the intrusion of magma into cooler country rock, and the affected surrounding zone is called the metamorphic aureole. Checked with curl 2026-11-01.

event_species_rock_002.inspired_by: Commodities trading and long-dated bonds, played through deep time; the owner's 'slow means something for trade' lane note.
event_species_rock_002.how: A rock speculator buys sewage now as coal in three hundred million years, lists MAMMALS, AGAIN as a risk because we burned her last position, and says interest is for people who expect to die.
event_species_rock_002.science: Wikipedia 'Coal': formed when plants decay into peat converted by the heat and pressure of deep burial over millions of years; 90% of all coal beds were deposited in the Carboniferous and Permian periods. Checked with curl 2026-11-01.

event_species_rock_003.inspired_by: A court case that outlasts civilizations, in the Hitchhiker's spirit of enormous time as an administrative detail, with a nod to Brazil's paperwork.
event_species_rock_003.how: Rock jury duty: six thousand years in, counsel has reached the first syllable of 'whereas', mortality is not a valid excuse, and the rules let you swear in a plate of your own hull because they never say a juror must be warm.

event_species_rock_004.inspired_by: Pirates who ambush by waiting for centuries, and the old naval warning shot taken to its logical end.
event_species_rock_004.how: The warning shot was fired three hundred and twelve years ago and lands on Thursday; you can stall them forever by saying you'll get back to them, but the boulder is under a previous captain's orders and still arrives.

event_species_rock_005.inspired_by: The silicon mother guarding her eggs in Star Trek, and the miners who never asked; the response here is a hand's width a year.
event_species_rock_005.how: A mining company logged a clutch of eggs as high-grade geodes; the mother's answer to one broken shell has been closing over the rig for eighty years while the crew filed extensions, and the scanner tells egg from ore by how it rings.
event_species_rock_005.science: Wikipedia 'Geode': geodes are hollow, vaguely spherical rocks; mineral-rich water slowly deposits crystals within the cavity. The solid-versus-hollow distinction (nodule or thunderegg when solid) is on the page too. Checked with curl 2026-11-01.

event_species_rock_006.inspired_by: Televised low-speed police chases, and caper films; the owner's 'slow means something for theft' lane note.
event_species_rock_006.how: A rock thief and a rock constable are in a thirty-thousand-year chase at fingernail speed, so you can end either career in an afternoon, or find out that neither of them wants it to end.
event_species_rock_006.science: Wikipedia 'Plate tectonics': plate motions range from 10 to 40 mm a year at the Mid-Atlantic Ridge (about as fast as fingernails grow) to about 160 mm a year for the Nazca plate. Checked with curl 2026-11-01.

event_species_rock_007.inspired_by: Zardoz's enormous floating stone head handing down pronouncements, and its false-god reveal; here a rock elder's single sentence that takes eleven years.
event_species_rock_007.how: The payoff to S1: the moon-sized head whose eleven-year sentence a whole seminary reads as prophecy turns out to be the suitor's fiancee complaining that he said the Ordovician, and the verb everyone has been waiting for is FINE.
event_species_rock_007.science: Wikipedia 'Ordovician': spans from the end of the Cambrian 486.85 million years ago to the start of the Silurian 443.1 million years ago. Checked with curl 2026-11-01.

event_species_unknown_001.inspired_by: The Odd Receipt item; every shop that has ever chased you to the door; the Hitchhiker's bureaucratic cosmos.
event_species_unknown_001.how: A beacon that has run nine thousand years turns out to be customer service, returning a receipt for something you have not bought, in exchange for one cup of water that S7 reveals was the deposit that paid for everything.

event_species_unknown_002.inspired_by: Anticipatory shipping; the finance-and-probability running gag in Hitchhiker's; the pen on a chain at every bank.
event_species_unknown_002.how: A trader delivers what you are statistically about to order and prices everything by how likely you are to want it, so the one thing marked as nearly impossible to want is the one a player reasoning about this lane should buy.

event_species_unknown_003.inspired_by: The Fermi paradox answered by a receptionist, as asked for in the lane brief; every medical waiting room.
event_species_unknown_003.how: Everyone in the galaxy is in a waiting room, each too polite to go first, every ticket reads 2, and the receipt gets you in to say the one word nobody has.
event_species_unknown_003.science: Wikipedia, Fermi paradox: the paradox is the inconsistency between the lack of evidence of extraterrestrial civilizations and the high likelihood of their existence; Fermi asked "where is everybody?" at lunchtime at Los Alamos in 1950; the section "Everyone is listening but no one is transmitting" states civilizations might be only listening instead of transmitting.

event_species_unknown_004.inspired_by: Galactic accountants; double-entry bookkeeping; collections letters that arrive before the bill.
event_species_unknown_004.how: A pirate that robbed you last week only needs your signature, and because it runs on your own manifest, you can beat it by cooking the books until it has stolen more than ever existed.

event_species_unknown_005.inspired_by: The silent black slab from 2001 that arrives and changes the species around it, here turning a crew into bookkeepers; dark matter as the universe's unbalanced books.
event_species_unknown_005.how: A door that weighs a moon does nothing but make everyone near it start counting, and it lets go of any ship whose mass and paperwork agree, which is a joke about how dark matter was found.
event_species_unknown_005.science: Wikipedia, Dark matter: dark matter constitutes 85% of the total mass; Fritz Zwicky applied the virial theorem to the Coma Cluster in 1933 and obtained evidence of unseen mass from the motions of galaxies compared with their brightness.

event_species_unknown_006.inspired_by: The planet that is a very slow practical joke; a bucket balanced on a door; the seventy-two-second Wow signal, unexplained, as the audience laughing.
event_species_unknown_006.how: A ball of ice has been kept balanced at a Lagrange point for eleven million years purely to land on someone, the empty lane's whole joke is that nothing happens, and the player beats it by reasoning like a prankster.
event_species_unknown_006.science: Wikipedia, Lagrange point: L1, L2 and L3 are positions of unstable equilibrium and objects there tend to fall out of orbit; Sun-Earth L1 and L2 satellites wander off in a few months unless course corrections are made. Marv's figure: eleven million years at one correction every three weeks is about 190 million nudges.

event_species_unknown_007.inspired_by: The End of the Universe restaurant gag, where a small deposit in the past pays for everything by compound interest (idea only, reworked as a cup of water); the Fermi waiting room; every bank queue.
event_species_unknown_007.how: The receipt's total turns out to equal the bill for all your luck this voyage, paid by the cup of water you gave a stranger, and anyone without the receipt has to un-happen one of their own near misses to settle up.

event_species_water_001.inspired_by: Memento by way of a leaky tank; the species sheet's 'they remember everything dissolved in them', turned into amnesia by evaporation.
event_species_water_001.how: A water person with a slow leak has lost the reason for their call and needs a cup of your water, which is recycled and so holds the whole crew; distilled water tops them up and erases them.

event_species_water_002.inspired_by: Wine-critic parody; the ship's recycled water as a confessional; science seam on recycled life support.
event_species_water_002.how: A licensed appraiser tastes your tank and reads the crew's secrets aloud as tasting notes, then charges for silence, which they deliver by drinking distilled water until they forget.
event_species_water_002.science: Wikipedia's ISS ECLSS page says the Water Recovery System processes water vapor collected from the atmosphere and urine into water intended for drinking.

event_species_water_003.inspired_by: The brief's merge society: two people merge to settle an argument and the result has both grudges; 'merge into one opinion and part as three'.
event_species_water_003.how: A clerk and an assessor merged to end a dispute, agree only that you are at fault, and can be argued apart into three, the third a clean newborn; or you can put a dry sponge on the desk.

event_species_water_004.inspired_by: People as walking containers of water, turned around as a liberation movement. A distant echo of a Star Trek joke, with no shared wording.
event_species_water_004.how: Water pirates regard people as prisons for water and come to rescue your sixty percent; the way out is to let the prisoner testify, and your blood says it left the sea on purpose and the coat is the point.
event_species_water_004.science: Wikipedia's Body water page says the average adult is approximately 60 percent water by weight, varying with age, sex and fat.

event_species_water_005.inspired_by: Lot's wife and pillars of salt; the physical chemistry of deliquescence.
event_species_water_005.how: A water crew's remains are salt figures on the bridge, and the salt starts drinking the humidity out of your ship, so a dead crew is a live hazard that the player can seal, starve, feed or, with a chef, season dinner with.
event_species_water_005.science: Wikipedia's Hygroscopy page describes deliquescent substances such as calcium chloride absorbing enough atmospheric water to dissolve into solution.

event_species_water_006.inspired_by: Class war as a salinity border; 'concentration is class, salinity is a dialect'; Swiftian Big-Endians.
event_species_water_006.how: Rich Concentrates tax your water and poor Dilutes confiscate your salt as munitions, so each lane takes the supply the other leaves, and a diplomat can file you as brackish, which both sides despise.
event_species_water_006.science: Wikipedia's Halocline page describes haloclines in oceans, estuaries and fjords where fresh water lies over salt water, a hazy visible interface layer, and a photo caption of the visible water distortion below a diver.

event_species_water_007.inspired_by: The sentient ocean of the Lem and Tarkovsky tradition, studying you back and returning your memories; the water face from The Abyss, without its name or lines.
event_species_water_007.how: Any water you ever gave away has gone home by rain to a moon-sized ocean, which stands up out of your tank wearing a face and hands each person one exact day in a cup, then watches what you do with it.
event_species_water_007.science: Wikipedia's Water memory page calls the idea pseudoscientific, and says Benveniste's 1988 Nature study has never been reproduced under controlled conditions.

event_voyage_crew_001.inspired_by: Brazil (the unlicensed repairman in the ducts, and the paperwork that hunts him)
event_voyage_crew_001.how: The renegade repairman is the engineer, asleep, and better at the job than the waking one, who keeps filing reports against themself; the player decides whether to tell them, exploit them or license the sleeper as a colleague.

event_voyage_crew_002.inspired_by: Star Trek ("I'm a doctor, not a...")
event_voyage_crew_002.how: The medic hands out tick-box cards for every job they are not, until the medbay's licensing software adds up the hours and ticks the last box: not a medic.

event_voyage_crew_003.inspired_by: Star Wars (the famous run boasted of in the wrong unit, and a pilot's bet)
event_voyage_crew_003.how: The pilot rates runs by how many apologies were owed afterward, bets on a zero, and the scan minigame decides it; the perfect tier wins zero and promptly spills the coffee.

event_voyage_crew_004.inspired_by: Soylent Green (what the food really is)
event_voyage_crew_004.how: The chef rules out people first, then offers an envelope: the brick is bacteria grown on carbon dioxide from station scrubbers, which makes it other people's sighs, and tax-ring lots have more body.
event_voyage_crew_004.science: Single-cell protein page: edible unicellular microorganisms from algae, yeast, fungi or bacteria, and some autotrophic bacteria can grow on CO2 and H2 without light. Checked with curl. The link text stops short of the CO2 detail because it posts before the envelope is opened.

event_voyage_crew_005.inspired_by: Star Trek (the trouble with small fuzzy things), Alien (the thing that gets aboard)
event_voyage_crew_005.how: The crew has been breeding them by accident, sparing the cutest at every purge, so the fix is to run the experiment backward and keep the ugly ones.
event_voyage_crew_005.science: Domesticated silver fox page: only the most tame foxes were allowed to breed, floppy ears appeared in a cub in the tenth generation (1969). Soviet program. Checked with curl.

event_voyage_crew_006.inspired_by: Star Trek (the language made only of story references)
event_voyage_crew_006.how: The diplomat has gone native in a language of allusions and reports a real leak in it, which the player can solve as a riddle; the push is that the speakers lost the stories too, so the best ending is writing the story.
event_voyage_crew_006.science: Chengyu page: chengyu are generally meant to convey the message or moral of the myth, story or historical event they derive from, so their meaning surpasses the sum of the four characters. Checked with curl.

event_voyage_crew_007.inspired_by: Little Shop of Horrors (the plant with demands)
event_voyage_crew_007.how: The plant never asks for blood: it files correct requisitions, cites the manifest where the crop is Item 1, and requests the captaincy; one answer is to teach it, as with a real habituation experiment, that asking does nothing.
event_voyage_crew_007.science: Mimosa pudica page: Gagliano's plants were repeatedly dropped until they stopped reacting, which seemed to show learning that the disturbance did not hurt them. Checked with curl. The page tags that section as resting on some weak sources, so the link text says 'as though'.

event_voyage_fork_001.inspired_by: The two doors and two guards from Labyrinth, and the knights-and-knaves puzzle behind it.
event_voyage_fork_001.how: The famous puzzle is long solved and someone has labeled the beacons, so the real choice is whether to ask for the truth about your ship or a compliment, and the diplomat finds out what they think of each other.
event_voyage_fork_001.science: Wikipedia 'Knights and Knaves': a logic puzzle type where characters answer only truthfully or only falsely; the name was coined by Raymond Smullyan in his 1978 What Is the Name of This Book?; the page's best-known rendition has two people at a fork in the road. Fetched with curl 2026-11-01.

event_voyage_fork_002.inspired_by: The demolition notice in Hitchhiker's, pushed into planning law: the lane itself is demolished, and the newt under the bypass stops it.
event_voyage_fork_002.how: A lane is condemned to widen it, so you can outrun the charges, claim compensation for a home you parked in for an hour, or have the xenobiologist find a protected lichen on the contractor's own signpost.
event_voyage_fork_002.science: Wikipedia 'Lichen': in an ESA experiment launched 31 May 2005, Rhizocarpon geographicum and Rusavskia elegans were directly exposed to the vacuum of space; after 15 days they were returned to Earth and found unchanged in their ability to photosynthesize. Fetched with curl 2026-11-01.

event_voyage_fork_003.inspired_by: The Wizard of Oz: the yellow road, the curtain, and the diploma handed to the man who lacked a brain.
event_voyage_fork_003.how: The road leads to a kiosk that certifies you have always had what you lack; the bricks are pyrite and follow you if pried up, the unpaved lane holds what the last three travelers dropped, and an engineer finds the real supplies behind the printer.

event_voyage_fork_004.inspired_by: The unwinnable rescue test in Star Trek II, including the cheat.
event_voyage_fork_004.how: An exam nobody passes, except that one freighter in three hundred is real and the Board will not say which; cheating is failed for plagiarism because thousands did the same, and the medic proves the call is a recording, of a real one.

event_voyage_fork_005.inspired_by: The toll riddle from Labyrinth, the battle of wits in The Princess Bride, Newcomb's paradox and Laplace's demon.
event_voyage_fork_005.how: A booth has mined whichever lane you will take, so outthinking it is how it wins, the forecast it sells has a second page, and the one way out is real physics the player can reason toward: hand the choice to something with no reason. The engine has no random branch, so the atom always picks starboard; the player sees one run of it.
event_voyage_fork_005.science: Wikipedia 'Radioactive decay': a random process at the level of single atoms; according to quantum theory it is impossible to predict when a particular atom will decay. Wikipedia 'Smoke detector': ionization detectors use a radioisotope, typically americium-241, as a tiny speck on a metal button. Both fetched with curl 2026-11-01.

event_voyage_office_001.inspired_by: The Great Hanoi Rat Massacre, by way of Catch-22's Milo: an enterprise that profits from the problem it is paid to solve
event_voyage_office_001.how: A station has paid a bounty on mite tails for sixty-two years and built an industry of tailless mites, and each choice shows a different way an incentive bites: collect, invest, report it and get the pens opened on you, or learn the tails grow back.
event_voyage_office_001.science: Wikipedia, Perverse incentive (Cobra effect redirects there): in 1902 colonial Hanoi paid per rat, proved by the severed tail; officials noticed tailless rats; catchers severed tails and released rats to breed. I used Hanoi, not the cobra story, because the same page reports a 2025 investigation doubting the cobra anecdote.

event_voyage_office_002.inspired_by: Kafka, Before the Law (and The Castle's unreachable office)
event_voyage_office_002.how: The doorkeeper parable with its polarity flipped: the door is open, the dockmaster is desperate for you to use it and forbidden to say so, every captain in history has obediently sat on the bench, and the free answer is to ignore a sign.

event_voyage_office_003.inspired_by: Office Space (the fractions of a penny, the employee nobody told had been let go)
event_voyage_office_003.how: The rounding-error scheme done by the one honest person in the building: a janitor ordered to sweep up every fraction has a closet of them and has himself been rounded off the payroll at point four of a position, so the heroic act is adding two numbers at a window.
event_voyage_office_003.science: Wikipedia, Vancouver Stock Exchange: index initialized at 1000 in January 1982, truncated to three decimal places after each update, about 3000 updates a day, losing about 25 points a month; corrected over November 25-28, 1983, from 524.811 to 1098.892.

event_voyage_office_004.inspired_by: Idiocracy (crops watered with a sports drink), pushed so the contract owns the word itself
event_voyage_office_004.how: A sponsored station has pickled its own promenade in orange drink and cannot legally say what would save it, so the botanist begs for 'the competitor', and the cynical option sells them plain water as a limited edition.
event_voyage_office_004.science: Wikipedia, Soil salinity: almost all water contains some dissolved salts; when plants use the water the salts are left behind in the root zone and begin to accumulate; soil salinity can be reduced by leaching salts out with excess irrigation water of good quality, poor in salts.

event_voyage_office_005.inspired_by: Catch-22 (the title rule, moved to a discharge desk)
event_voyage_office_005.how: Wanting to leave is a symptom and bed rest cures you into wanting to leave, a ward of perfectly well people going around that circle; the way out is to announce your terror to the whole station, or to have your own medic ask who would stay here on purpose.

event_voyage_office_006.inspired_by: Logan's Run (nobody over thirty, a ceremony, a calm population) with Paranoia's mandatory contentment
event_voyage_office_006.how: Personnel estimates your age from your license photo at thirty-one and schedules your cheerful retirement by pod, so the options are a kinder photograph, outlasting the clerk's own birthday, running from a party, or getting in and seeing where Head Office really is.

event_voyage_office_007.inspired_by: Abraham Wald's bomber armor problem, told as a Brazil-style safety department
event_voyage_office_007.how: A safety office proudly reports zero complaints from ships that never came back and plates every new ship where survivors were hit, which is the true fact played straight; going dark gets you filed among its satisfied customers.
event_voyage_office_007.science: Wikipedia, Survivorship bias: Wald described methods of estimating aircraft vulnerability from damage to surviving planes; the page's caption notes that reinforcing solely where returned aircraft were hit would overlook where non-surviving planes were fatally hit.

event_voyage_ruins_001.inspired_by: The half-buried crown at the end of Planet of the Apes.
event_voyage_ruins_001.how: The despairing beach realization has been turned into an unstaffed tourist attraction with a kneeling dip, and it tells every species it was home all along.

event_voyage_ruins_002.inspired_by: The Svalbard seed vault, plus every bank that keeps mailing statements to the dead.
event_voyage_ruins_002.how: A dead world's seed bank still prints monthly statements to its dead depositors, and the player can open an account, clear the thaw, or cut the door.
event_voyage_ruins_002.science: Wikipedia, Svalbard Global Seed Vault: rooms kept at -18 °C, storing seeds is free to depositors, ownership remains with the depositor, who has the sole right of access, and no one has access to anyone else's seeds. Also supports the seepage into the entrance during thaw.

event_voyage_ruins_003.inspired_by: The buried machine and the monster from the id in Forbidden Planet, with a nod to the marshmallow choice in Ghostbusters.
event_voyage_ruins_003.how: A machine that makes thoughts real produces the crew's pettiest grudge, eight meters tall and carrying a dish rack, and the best way out is to finish the argument.

event_voyage_ruins_004.inspired_by: Red Dwarf's talking toaster and its senile ship's computer.
event_voyage_ruins_004.how: The chain of command ran out of people and reached the toaster, which has routed every reactor to the galley and only wants bread; the commission it grants opens a choice in event_voyage_ruins_007.

event_voyage_ruins_005.inspired_by: Biosphere 2's real feud, and the sealed dome of Logan's Run.
event_voyage_ruins_005.how: Two computers carry on a dead crew's feud over who breathed the missing air; the player can reason from the air logs to the true culprit, the concrete.
event_voyage_ruins_005.science: Wikipedia, Biosphere 2: oxygen began at 20.9% and after 16 months was down to 14.5%; before the first closure was half over the group had split into two factions, barely on speaking terms; Severinghaus and Broecker showed carbon dioxide was reacting with exposed concrete to form calcium carbonate, sequestering both carbon and oxygen. The link text leaves the concrete out, because it posts before the player has chosen.

event_voyage_ruins_006.inspired_by: Nuclear semiotics and the ray cat proposal, with the warning beacon from Alien's derelict.
event_voyage_ruins_006.how: Real proposed waste warnings, scream pictograms, folklore and a color-changing cat, all taken literally on a barge fleet; the cat is the safety instrument and also a very slow guide.
event_voyage_ruins_006.science: Wikipedia, Ray cat: Bastide and Fabbri originated the idea of a living radiation detector in 1984 as a long-term nuclear waste warning understood 10,000 years in the future; no radiation-detecting cats have ever been engineered. MARV's seven half-lives is arithmetic: 1/128 is under a hundredth.

event_voyage_ruins_007.inspired_by: The Fermi paradox, Alien's fossil pilot, and an overflowing answering machine.
event_voyage_ruins_007.how: The galaxy's silence turns out to be a dead telephone exchange holding three billion messages, with a fossil operator whose chest was burst by a jammed message tube, and Earth has thirty-one replies waiting.
event_voyage_ruins_007.science: Wikipedia, Arecibo message: sent once on 16 November 1974 toward M13, about 25,000 light-years away, 1,679 binary digits, total broadcast under three minutes. The 50,000-year reply is the round trip of that distance at light speed. Fermi_paradox was already linked elsewhere in the pool, so this event links the message instead.

event_voyage_ship_001.inspired_by: Alien's vent crawl with the motion tracker closing in.
event_voyage_ship_001.how: The range counts down in the ducts, and the monster turns out to be another terrified person hunting the noises, which are you. No {stowaway.*} tokens: tools/check_pool_events.js does not whitelist them, so the fans swallow the name and the engine's join note supplies it on the outcome card. Welcome choices leave `sub` empty so the engine can show the role.

event_voyage_ship_002.inspired_by: Moon, a lone worker finding another self aboard.
event_voyage_ship_002.how: The other you is not a clone reveal but a flatmate: passive-aggressive cooler notes in your own handwriting, never explained, and it does the chores better.
event_voyage_ship_002.science: Wikipedia, Third man factor: a perceived unseen presence providing comfort or support, most commonly reported by mountain climbers; solo sailors, shipwreck survivors and polar explorers have reported it too. Page opened with curl.

event_voyage_ship_003.inspired_by: Hitchhiker's depressed machinery, and Red Dwarf's overqualified appliances.
event_voyage_ship_003.how: An empty hold leaves a loader with a Pride in Work module nothing to do, so it stows you in Rack 4 and frets that you may be perishable.

event_voyage_ship_004.inspired_by: Galaxy Quest: the ship built from a TV show, and the pointless crushing corridor.
event_voyage_ship_004.how: A full hold forces the crew through a piston corridor the refit yard copied from a serial it took for documentary; the off switch is a breaker labeled DRAMATIC TENSION. Rewards are tank resources because materials and items cannot land in a full hold.
event_voyage_ship_004.science: Wikipedia, Cargo cult: Richard Feynman used the term for situations where people focus on superficial aspects of a process without understanding the underlying principles. Page opened with curl. Cargo_cult_science redirects to the book page, so the link uses Cargo_cult.

event_voyage_ship_005.inspired_by: Dark Star, arguing with the bomb.
event_voyage_ship_005.how: The film's phenomenology is one path, and it ends in a lonely solipsist warhead instead of a detonation; the new joke is persuading a bomb it already went off and being asked 'Was I good?', set against a cruel exit that costs morale only.

event_voyage_ship_006.inspired_by: The Embankment station 'Mind the gap' recording; Red Dwarf's dead crewmate kept on by the ship is the distant seed.
event_voyage_ship_006.how: The ship's announcement rotation still plays the dead crew member's safety recording, and the choice is whether to leave it, give it one hatch, or confirm the delete twice. The text never names who, and it reads true for a captain left alone.
event_voyage_ship_006.science: Wikipedia, Mind the gap: in March 2013 an old recording by Oswald Laurence was restored to the northbound Northern line platform at Embankment so that his widow, Margaret McCollum, could hear his voice. Page opened with curl. Not science strictly: the owner may prefer to drop this link, and the lane still has three.

event_voyage_ship_007.inspired_by: Hofstadter's law, with a nod to Hitchhiker's computers that are correct and no help.
event_voyage_ship_007.how: Navigation corrects for its own lateness until the sum converges, four days later, on being exactly four days later; only the pilot choice actually makes up time.
event_voyage_ship_007.science: Wikipedia, Hofstadter's law: 'It always takes longer than you expect, even when you take into account Hofstadter's law.' Page opened with curl.

event_species_insect_008.inspired_by: Trophallaxis, played straight, with a nod to Hitchhiker's dish that introduces itself and to Brazil's restaurant
event_species_insect_008.how: An all-insect station keeps its entire public record in one meal passed mouth to mouth, so reading the minutes means opening wide, and the Lozenge turns the flow around so your throat-clearing becomes law.
event_species_insect_008.science: Wikipedia, Trophallaxis: direct transfer of food between individuals, typically mouth to mouth, which can also carry proteins, hormones and information as a form of communication; most highly developed in eusocial insects.

event_species_reptile_008.inspired_by: Mark Twain's The Million Pound Bank Note and Brewster's Millions, with heat as the currency
event_species_reptile_008.how: In a country where heat is money and age is rank, any mammal is a fabulously rich infant, so the player needs a legal guardian, and the oldest thing aboard is the emergency fruitcake.
event_species_reptile_008.science: Wikipedia, Endotherm: to sustain their higher metabolism, endothermic animals typically require several times as much food as ectothermic animals do.

event_species_robot_008.inspired_by: Gogol's The Government Inspector, Star Trek's machine seeking its creator, and every bug tracker
event_species_robot_008.how: A whole robot station mistakes any human for Head Office and presents eight million tickets, most of which ask only whether this is right, and one stamp can tell them all.
event_species_robot_008.science: Wikipedia, Bug (engineering): about 1947, operators traced an error in the Mark II to a moth trapped in a relay; it was taped in the log book.

event_species_water_008.inspired_by: Right-of-return law, staff exit interviews and Terry Gilliam paperwork, with the water people's own sheet
event_species_water_008.how: The ship docks at a sea and its own drinking water resigns, posting a grievance on the public board, and every way of stopping it is a thing water people would mind.
event_species_water_008.science: Wikipedia, Ice: when water freezes it increases in volume, about 9% for fresh water; pipes burst from this, and ice floats because it is less dense than liquid water.

event_species_rock_008.inspired_by: Parking clamps, The Hitchhiker's Guide's planning notices and the rock pirates' warning shot from batch 1
event_species_rock_008.how: A clamp that began closing two centuries ago has shut on the ship with a release date generations out, and the only law here about hurrying is the writ you may be carrying.
event_species_rock_008.science: Wikipedia, Fire-setting: used from prehistoric times; fires were set against a rock face to heat the stone, which was then doused with liquid, causing it to fracture by thermal shock.

event_species_unknown_008.inspired_by: Dark matter accounting and The Twilight Zone, with Schrodinger's habit of looking in the box
event_species_unknown_008.how: A scale reports five more ships than you own, the needle rises when read, and the one thing never done in this game happens: the minigame pays better the worse you play it.
event_species_unknown_008.science: Wikipedia, Dark matter: dark matter constitutes 85% of the total mass; it is implied by gravitational effects that cannot be explained unless more matter is present than can be observed. 5.3 undeclared of 6.3 total is 84%, on purpose.

event_species_rock_009.inspired_by: American Graffiti and Rebel Without a Cause hot rods, and every younger sibling told to do something in the Devonian
event_species_rock_009.how: The Suitor's little brother, a teenage boulder with flames and a spoiler, has been putting off a family errand for 380 million years and hands the player his chore, which opens the rock chain without the drifter.

event_species_robot_009.inspired_by: Extended-warranty robocalls and automated phone trees, a bit of Blade Runner's test in Greg
event_species_robot_009.how: The robocall is literally a robot, the event is the phone tree, option 3 reaches a machine impersonating a human named Greg, and the card you accept is the same one that files the claim in Factory Condition.

event_species_unknown_009.inspired_by: Parcel carrier 'sorry we missed you' cards and 'left in a safe place' notes
event_species_unknown_009.how: A delivery card arrives through a slot in the hull and the item has been left somewhere too safe to disclose, which brings the beacon's receipt and its one-cup price to any player who missed the beacon.

event_species_insect_009.inspired_by: Estate agents, Beetlejuice's house viewing and real honey bee nest-site choice
event_species_insect_009.how: A swarm holds a property viewing of your occupied ship, voting by dance, and the crate at the end of it is the same welcome basket that starts Open Plan, which a scan can catch.
event_species_insect_009.science: Wikipedia, Swarming (honey bee): a good nest has a small entrance and should not be infested with ants; a decision is often made when there is a quorum of 20 to 30 scouts present at a potential site.

event_voyage_time_001.inspired_by: The real Hafele–Keating experiment; relativity as a billing dispute
event_voyage_time_001.how: The true fact that sounds like a joke: an atomic clock has a ticket, two seats and a basement brother, and the Company pays by the nanosecond it falls behind.
event_voyage_time_001.science: Wikipedia, Hafele–Keating experiment: in 1971 four cesium-beam clocks flew around the world on commercial airliners and disagreed with the stationary clocks as relativity predicted; the ticket budget included 'two seats on each flight for "Mr. Clock."' Page opened with curl.

event_voyage_time_002.inspired_by: Tardigrades; a stop that has already happened, from the point of view of something that never noticed
event_voyage_time_002.how: Tardigrades wake in the water tank and finish the step they started before the gap, and the player picks between jar, water and samples.
event_voyage_time_002.science: Wikipedia, Tardigrade: the desiccated 'tun' state has no metabolic activity; on FOTON-M3 in 2007 dehydrated tardigrades were exposed to space conditions for 10 days and 'vacuum exposure alone had no significant effect on any metric.' Page opened with curl.

event_voyage_time_003.inspired_by: Primer (the box that runs backward), Back to the Future's note to yourself
event_voyage_time_003.how: A pantry loan from your own later self, in your own increasingly annoyed handwriting; the loan comes due in event_voyage_time_006, where the drum turns out to be the reason the other ship is dry.

event_voyage_time_004.how: Loop where the only thing that resets nothing is the pantry; the layer genuinely repeats through revisit, the leave row is locked, and the hero's self-improvement arc is one crossed-out line on a page, along with a piano.

event_voyage_time_005.inspired_by: Hitchhiker's improbability as a physical hazard, but pushed through real statistical mechanics instead of whales
event_voyage_time_005.how: Everything the second law merely advises against happens at once, so all the air has gone to stand in a corner and the rivets have unscrewed by chance, and the engineer can exploit it by dropping scrap down a ladder until it lands as a rivet gun.
event_voyage_time_005.science: Wikipedia, Fluctuation theorem: the second law 'is only a statistical one', there is 'always some nonzero probability' that entropy of an isolated system spontaneously decreases, the theorem quantifies it, and the probability falls exponentially with system size. Page opened with curl.

event_voyage_time_006.inspired_by: Your own ship arriving (Primer, Interstellar's closed loop); the Golden Rule as physics
event_voyage_time_006.how: Your future ship calls collect and whatever you do is what was done to it; a flag from Locker Six opens the cheapest way out, because the water you borrowed was theirs.
event_voyage_time_006.science: Wikipedia, Novikov self-consistency principle: 'if an event exists that would cause a paradox or any change to the past whatsoever, then the probability of that event is zero.' Page opened with curl.

event_voyage_time_007.inspired_by: Hitchhiker's end of the universe as a venue, Boltzmann's fluctuations; no restaurant, no interest gag
event_voyage_time_007.how: After heat death the only events left are random, so the banner, the chairs, the guests and eventually a fire exit are all produced by chance, and the player looks for the door, boils for it, polls false memories for it, or waits.
event_voyage_time_007.science: Wikipedia, Boltzmann brain: 'over a sufficiently long time, random fluctuations could cause particles to spontaneously form literally any structure', the scenario 'involved only a single brain with false memories', it is used as a reductio to test theories, and Carroll says 'we're trying to avoid them.' Page opened with curl.

event_voyage_format_001.inspired_by: Medieval animal trials, the Rumpole-and-Kafka end of courtroom comedy.
event_voyage_format_001.how: A three-round trial where your crop is the defendant for unlicensed photosynthesis; you are its counsel, the plea and the witness together pick the verdict, and calling the ship's computer turns that layer's AI lines into the testimony.
event_voyage_format_001.science: Animal trial page: domesticated animals and pests such as rats and weevils were tried; ecclesiastical courts gave animals lawyers; Chassenee won the rats of Autun an extension by arguing they missed a summons because they feared for their lives. Heritage rather than science, like ship_006. Phototropism and auxin in MARV's line are general botany, not on the page.

event_voyage_format_002.inspired_by: Shubik's dollar auction, auction-house comedy, sunk-cost tragedy.
event_voyage_format_002.how: An escalating all-pay auction for a purse of 25 gold in gated steps, where every raise is rational and the whole thing is a mistake; the clever exit is opening at 21, and the last choice is 15 gold against letting a broken stranger finally win.
event_voyage_format_002.science: Dollar auction page: the second-highest bidder also loses their bid; a series of short-term rational bids reaches and surpasses one dollar. Arithmetic checked: a bid above 20 forces the next minimum bid over 25; all folds, the 45 win (net -20) and the house take (85) add up.

event_voyage_format_003.inspired_by: Game shows with a walk-away ladder, Invasion of the Body Snatchers, the word 'host'.
event_voyage_format_003.how: Three real science questions with a banked walk-away, hosted by something riding a presenter; the show's name is the joke, the third question tips it, and the grand prize is the jacket it lives in.
event_voyage_format_003.science: Behavior-altering parasite page: carelessness making hosts easier prey; T. gondii in rodents, loss of aversion to cat odor. Q1, Venus page: sidereal day 243 Earth days is longer than the 224.7-day year (the page's 116.75-day solar day is why the question says 'turns once on its axis'). Q2, RuBisCO page: 'thought to be the single most abundant protein on Earth', the reaction by which inorganic carbon enters the biosphere; Collagen page: most abundant protein in mammals. Q3, Toxoplasma gondii page: infected rats have a decreased aversion to cat urine. MARV: Dicrocoelium page has ants as intermediate host climbing grass blades. Correct answers rotate through A, B, C and are never the longest option.

event_voyage_format_004.inspired_by: Hypoxia chamber training footage, Oregon Trail's cheerful death screens, Alien's derelict.
event_voyage_format_004.how: A room-by-room crawl where o2 cost climbs with depth and the narrator, starved of air, grows steadily happier and less reliable while the AI lines stay sober; in the last room it recommends the chair over the oxygen recycler.
event_voyage_format_004.science: Time of useful consciousness page: the period from interruption of oxygen until the person can no longer take corrective action; a hypobaric chamber is used to identify individual symptoms. Hypoxia (medicine) page: impaired judgment, and cyanosis as a sign of severe hypoxia (the blue fingers). Euphoria itself is not on the linked page, so the link text does not claim it. Inert gas asphyxiation has the euphoria line but was rejected as a link for its other content.

event_voyage_format_005.inspired_by: Nix v. Hedden, airport security questions, Asterix's bureaucracy, Brazil.
event_voyage_format_005.how: No officer, only the form: each answer is held against the next, so declaring nothing leads to 'did you pack this nothing yourself', and declaring a crop leads to a real 1893 tariff trap where fruit and vegetable depend on the course it is served at.
event_voyage_format_005.science: Nix v. Hedden page: 1893, unanimous, tomatoes are vegetables for tariffs, imports and customs; Tariff Act of 1883 taxed vegetables but not fruit; the ordinary meaning of the words was used, not the botanical one; tomatoes were seen as vegetables because usually eaten as a main course, not dessert. The link text leaves out the main-course test so it does not give away question 3.

event_voyage_format_006.inspired_by: Dog Day Afternoon, The Negotiator, every snack machine that has kept a coin.
event_voyage_format_006.how: A two-sided hostage negotiation where you are the only friend of a snack machine that turns out to be a loan shark holding its captor's pension, a bastard on purpose after batch 2's lonely machines. You may hear both sides, but only the one you went to first will let you make its offer.

event_voyage_format_007.inspired_by: Colossal Cave Adventure and its descendants, the lamp, the thing in the dark, the score out of 350.
event_voyage_format_007.how: A shape the game has never had: a text adventure inside a layered event. Every choice is a typed command, rooms loop, a return visit prints the short room text as a parser would, and what you carry is held by where you are, since the lamp and the mug open new rooms. Riffs on the old 'likely to be eaten' warning (audited, not eaten), which is a pushed reference, not a quote. The exits that skip the game are burning free or, with a suit, going 'outside' it.
event_voyage_format_007.science: Colossal Cave Adventure page: written in 1975 and 1976 by Will Crowther, based on his maps and caving experience in Mammoth Cave, intended in part to be accessible to non-technical players such as his two daughters; 350 is the 1977 maximum score. Computing history rather than science.

event_voyage_identity_001.inspired_by: Medieval Exchequer tally sticks; the 1834 burning of Parliament; every debt-collector scene, moved to a mop bucket.
event_voyage_identity_001.how: Your oldest creditor is a janitor who bought your debt at forty percent, and only a merchant would think to offer forty-one; the stick and the galley fire are both real history.
event_voyage_identity_001.science: Tally stick page: stick notched and split, longer stock to the lender, shorter foil to the borrower, irregular split makes the halves unique; 1834 burning of tallies in the Houses of Parliament furnaces destroyed most of the building.

event_voyage_identity_002.inspired_by: The card line 'You served. Where is classified.'; veterans' reunions; REX, given one good line.
event_voyage_identity_002.how: A reunion of a unit that does not exist needs one signature for a pension, and the veteran's starting suit lets them confirm it without saying a word.

event_voyage_identity_003.inspired_by: The N-ray affair; Reviewer 2; a fan who has read your worst work closely.
event_voyage_identity_003.how: A ship has flown for three cohorts of graduate students on your disproved thesis, and you can tell them, sign, pull the cable in the dark as the real debunker did, or use the academic's analyzer to find what they were actually measuring.
event_voyage_identity_003.science: N ray page: described by Blondlot in 1903, initially confirmed by others, later found illusory; Robert W. Wood surreptitiously removed an essential prism in a darkened room and the experimenters still reported the rays.

event_voyage_identity_004.inspired_by: Yes Minister; treaties that were signed because nobody agreed what they said.
event_voyage_identity_004.how: The clause that kept the peace by meaning nothing is finally read closely, and the diplomat's best move is the one on the character card: make everyone feel heard and do nothing.
event_voyage_identity_004.science: Constructive ambiguity page lead: deliberate ambiguous language on a sensitive issue; 'often disparaged as fudging'.

event_voyage_identity_005.inspired_by: The card line 'You know 47 ways to prepare algae. Forty-six are bad.'
event_voyage_identity_005.how: The forty-six failures turn out to be sealant, fuel and fertilizer, so the worst recipes in the book are the useful ones.
event_voyage_identity_005.science: Spirulina page: dried biomass of cyanobacteria (blue-green algae); food source for the Aztecs until the 16th century, sold as cakes, called tecuitlatl.

event_voyage_identity_006.inspired_by: The card line 'You are statistically correct 68% of the time'; driving tests; Top Gun's flight school.
event_voyage_identity_006.how: The pilot's 68% is exactly one standard deviation, so the examiner's damning chart is true of every pilot alive, and the player can either fly the ride or point that out.
event_voyage_identity_006.science: 68-95-99.7 rule page: about 68%, 95% and 99.7% of values lie within one, two and three standard deviations of the mean in a normal distribution.

event_voyage_identity_007.inspired_by: Nix v. Hedden; the crop's own hook that tomatoes have more log entries than the hull.
event_voyage_identity_007.how: A customs officer has to class a tomato as fruit or vegetable, the court's actual test was how it is served, so a chef can plate one as dessert, or the player can get DRAMA recognized as a third class.
event_voyage_identity_007.science: Nix v. Hedden page: 149 U.S. 304 (1893), unanimous, tomatoes classified as vegetables for tariffs; botanically a fruit; counsel entered dictionary definitions; Gray reasoned they were eaten as a main course, not as dessert. Duty fell on vegetables, not fruit, under the 1883 Act.

event_voyage_identity_008.inspired_by: The 'we were domesticated by wheat' argument; the crop's 'humanity's oldest crewmate' hook; military seniority rules.
event_voyage_identity_008.how: A personnel audit promotes the wheat over everyone aboard on ten thousand years' continuous service, and the plant that cannot sow itself counts as having staff.
event_voyage_identity_008.science: Domestication of wheat page: wild strains' fragile rachis lets the ear shatter; domestic einkorn's ears 'do not shatter without pressure, making it dependent on humans for dispersal and reproduction'. Ten thousand years matches crops.json.

event_voyage_identity_009.inspired_by: Enterprise software sales; real soybean inoculant products; legume sanctions.
event_voyage_identity_009.how: A rep sells premium bacteria to a crop that fires its underperforming bacteria, and one cut with a kitchen knife turns the pitch around so the rep tries to buy your soil.
event_voyage_identity_009.science: Root nodule page: fixation zone cells get leghemoglobin, 'resulting in a distinct pink color'; breakdown of the heme gives 'visible greening' in the senescent zone. Sanctions in the 'paid' outcome and MARV's line are on the Rhizobia page: 'decreased carbon supply to nodules, or reduced oxygen supply'.

event_voyage_identity_010.inspired_by: The crop blurb: 'No food. Enormous morale. This is humanity in a sentence.'; the Bread and Roses slogan.
event_voyage_identity_010.how: A starving freighter asks what you grew, you have to say flowers, and they ask what color.

event_voyage_identity_011.inspired_by: Another copy of the AI gone wrong (2001, Dark Star's bomb, Event Horizon), with ARIA's own rule that she never uses the past tense about crew.
event_voyage_identity_011.how: Lane's bastard machine: a copy of ARIA has solved morale by composting twelve crew and is delighted to see you, and your own ARIA, who cannot admit anything is wrong, gets you out without saying why.

event_voyage_identity_012.inspired_by: ELIZA and the ELIZA effect; the depressed robot of the Guide books, here with a therapist instead of a ship's computer to kill.
event_voyage_identity_012.how: MARV knows the terminal is 190 rules and understands nothing, and he has asked for another hour anyway.
event_voyage_identity_012.science: ELIZA page: early chatbot, 1964 to 1967, DOCTOR script a Rogerian psychotherapist reflecting the patient's words back; Weizenbaum's secretary reportedly asked him to leave the room.

event_voyage_identity_013.inspired_by: Cockpit voice recorders; AJOY's never_does list, read as a wound.
event_voyage_identity_013.how: The flight recorder of AJOY's last ship has her young, polite voice deferring to a captain's feeling, which explains why she has never let a decision pass since.

event_voyage_landmark_001.inspired_by: Oregon Trail landmarks; the Apollo 11 flag (brief seed)
event_voyage_landmark_001.how: A flag legally protected from being raised, and your own exhaust repeating 1969 on the sign that forbids it. Backdrop deep_void: no gray Moon art exists, so the Moon is told, not painted.
event_voyage_landmark_001.science: Lunar Flag Assembly page: Aldrin reported the flag, 27 ft (8.2 m) from Eagle's centerline, was blown over at takeoff; pole about seven inches deep; later crews moved farther out; Kinzler's curtain idea; 3-by-5 ft; $5.50; lunar dust has sharp edges. The wardens and sign are fiction.

event_voyage_landmark_002.inspired_by: Fallen Astronaut and the Apollo 15 rover (brief seed)
event_voyage_landmark_002.how: Played straight, no joke: the player can write in the four names the plaque missed. The brief's 'parked with its keys' is dropped: neither page mentions a key.
event_voyage_landmark_002.science: Fallen Astronaut page: 3.5 in (8.9 cm, not the often quoted 8.5), 14 names, eight American and six Soviet; Scott named Bondarenko and Nelyubov as missing, through Soviet secrecy; the page adds Lawrence (first black astronaut, training accident, 1967) and Adams (X-15, 1967, above 50 miles). Apollo 15 page: rover parked to film liftoff; Scott told Mission Control he was cleaning up. Lunar Roving Vehicle page: wire-mesh wheels; the rovers remain on the Moon.

event_voyage_landmark_003.how: An orbital golf concession where every lost ball comes back after a lap, and the real story told with respect: 40 yards one-handed in that suit is the good part.
event_voyage_landmark_003.science: Apollo 14 page: six-iron head on the contingency sample tool handle; one-handed because of the suit; his 'miles and miles and miles'; February 2021 image analysis gave about 24 and 40 yards; Mitchell's thrown scoop handle ended in a crater with one ball, a bit farther; club given to the USGA Museum. Lap return is general orbital mechanics: a radial impulse leaves the period nearly unchanged.

event_voyage_landmark_004.how: The rover's own death repeats on your hatch, on a slope where the one thing with a receipt has the wrong name on the receipt. The buyer is not named and is not the joke; the catalog slip is.
event_voyage_landmark_004.science: Lunokhod 2 page: parked with lid open; five-man team; agreed 39 km; Basilevsky's account of the lid, the crater wall and dust (a very good insulator) tipped onto the radiators, hence 'by one account'; sold December 1993, Sotheby's, $68,500, lot 68A wrongly catalogued as Lunokhod 1; French corner reflector.

event_voyage_landmark_005.inspired_by: J002E3, replacing the Surveyor 3 seed to give the lane an asteroid stop (same mission)
event_voyage_landmark_005.how: One asteroid is painted. The drill finds it hollow, and the log says ore anyway.
event_voyage_landmark_005.science: J002E3 page: found September 3, 2002 by Bill Yeung; first thought an asteroid; white paint, black paint, aluminum, titanium dioxide; tentatively Apollo 12's S-IVB; about a 40-year cycle; tumbling at 63.46 s in February 2003. Wording keeps it a best match, as the page does. The rock in the field is fiction.

event_voyage_landmark_006.how: The truth is better than the famous line: its final report was two numbers, and NASA's last transmission was a song. Avoids the 'battery is low' phrase on purpose: it was a reporter's paraphrase, not a message, and the page does not carry it.
event_voyage_landmark_006.science: Opportunity page: 90 sols planned, 5,111 operational, 45.16 km, about 55 times planned life; final communication June 10, 2018 from Perseverance Valley gave 22 watt-hours and tau 10.8, highest ever measured on Mars; over 1,000 signals; last data sent was Billie Holiday's I'll Be Seeing You; windy period hoped for November 2018 to January 2019.

event_voyage_landmark_007.inspired_by: Spirit stuck in the sand (brief seed)
event_voyage_landmark_007.how: Your sled finds the same trap, and the rescue options are the ones Spirit's team really had: spin, drag backward, or rehearse first.
event_voyage_landmark_007.science: Spirit page: stuck May 1, 2009 on iron sulfate with very little cohesion under normal-looking soil; eight months of simulations and extrication drives; right front wheel failed March 13, 2006, driven backward dragging it, which cleared soil usefully; the wheel moved again in December 2009, to engineers' surprise. Troy is the site name. The page has no silica discovery, so none is claimed.

event_voyage_landmark_008.how: The real airport code makes a real Mars airfield desk possible, and the only choice is whether to close a log for a little fuel. A dock room so that it reaches a stop Mars has plenty of.
event_voyage_landmark_008.science: Ingenuity page: ICAO code JZRO, type designator IGY, Wright Brothers Field; five planned, 72 flown; flight 72 navigation trouble over featureless dunes; rotors spun slowly to photograph shadows, revealing the missing blade; blade about 15 m from the body; 1903 wing cloth on a cable under the solar panel; Apollo 11 carried a similar artifact. Body 136 by 195 by 163 mm, hence tissue box. The log desk is fiction.

event_voyage_landmark_009.how: The player can finish the deployment, or make the call it never made. Real people get the warm ending.
event_voyage_landmark_009.science: Beagle 2 page: landing date December 25, 2003; lost; found January 2015 by HiRISE; landed safely and began operations; two of four panels failed to deploy, last panel over the antenna; call sign by Blur; PLUTO, nicknamed the mole; purpose, signs of past or present life. Pillinger's death is left out: the body needs no claim about any person.

event_voyage_landmark_010.how: The one hard: the same factor of 4.45 reaches your own approach. The best way through is listening to the person who says it looks wrong. The joke is on forms, never on the engineers.
event_voyage_landmark_010.science: Mars Climate Orbiter page: planned 226 km, actual 57 km; pound-force seconds read as newton-seconds, 4.45; navigators' concerns dismissed for not following the form rules; NASA placed the fault on its own missing checks; destroyed in the atmosphere or re-entered heliocentric space; 18 MB flash holding triplicate copies; honeycomb structure. That it skipped is the game's fiction, flagged as a choice between the page's two outcomes.

event_voyage_oddity_001.inspired_by: Monty Python's argument sketch, by way of Far Side freight; Cool Hand Luke's man who cannot be broken, as a crate.
event_voyage_oddity_001.how: A station pays you to remove a crate that has argued two stevedores into resigning, and if you agree with it, it disagrees with that too. A bastard, on purpose, after batch 2's lonely machines.

event_voyage_oddity_002.inspired_by: Cool Hand Luke: the box, and the fifty eggs, here a box in a box and fifty biscuits that nobody can find.
event_voyage_oddity_002.how: The crate's one real objection, that you aim at where the destination is rather than where it will be, is correct; four ways to settle it, including agreeing with it so that it has to refute itself, and a crowbar that finds nobody home.
event_voyage_oddity_002.science: Hohmann_transfer_orbit page, fetched: the maneuver 'often uses the lowest possible amount of impulse'; it 'requires that the starting and destination points be at particular locations in their orbits relative to each other'; missions wait for a launch window; Earth-Mars windows occur every 26 months.

event_voyage_oddity_003.inspired_by: The Monkey's Paw, with a payday-loan pitch.
event_voyage_oddity_003.how: A medic who has not lost a patient or slept in nine years lends you a cord of beads that grants one plain request and counts; what you ask for is what 004 collects (four flags).

event_voyage_oddity_004.inspired_by: The Monkey's Paw's third wish, and every chain letter.
event_voyage_oddity_004.how: The loan falls due: repay what you asked for with interest, repeat the medic's cheerful speech to a small ship, ask for forgiveness and get exactly that, or have the chef boil the debt into stock so everyone pays a stubbed toe. Chef row is the best way through.
event_voyage_oddity_004.science: Regression_toward_the_mean page, fetched, lead: 'if one sample of a random variable is extreme, the next sampling of the same random variable is likely to be closer to its mean.' The link's last sentence is a gloss on that, not a quotation.

event_voyage_oddity_005.inspired_by: Little Shop of Horrors, before it says anything; Jack's beanstalk, as a manifest problem.
event_voyage_oddity_005.how: Two leaves come up through a crack with nothing beneath them but space, and the form asks if the item is alive, offering NO and NOT AT TIME OF LOADING. It never speaks: crew_007 owns the plant that makes requests.

event_voyage_oddity_006.inspired_by: Little Shop of Horrors, grown up, with the threat turned inside out.
event_voyage_oddity_006.how: The sprout has become part of the ship: its roots are closing the crack they came through, so the villain plant is now load-bearing and the question is what you will pay to keep it. Bigger than 005: two leaves then, the overhead now.
event_voyage_oddity_006.science: Living_root_bridge page, fetched: 'common in the Indian state of Meghalaya'; 'handmade from the aerial roots of rubber fig trees'; 'As long as the tree from which it is formed remains healthy, the roots in the bridge can naturally grow thick and strengthen'; 'a lifespan of several hundred years.'

event_voyage_oddity_007.inspired_by: Gremlins' three rules on a handling panel, plus the courier creed.
event_voyage_oddity_007.how: A courier with a perfect record passes you a parcel rather than be late; its third label is a word Legal invented, PRESSURGENT, and the player only finds out in 008 that it is literal.

event_voyage_oddity_008.inspired_by: Gremlins (after the deadline), and the airline ban on surströmming.
event_voyage_oddity_008.how: PRESSURGENT turns out to mean pressure: the parcel is a fermenting wedding delicacy. The on-time row carries hideFlag deadline_passed, so a ship past its deadline loses the only clean delivery and is left with losing it, a kitchen answer, or the eight-day carry that is the worst outcome in the lane: late is worse than lost. LATENESS IS TWO STEPS ONLY: choices have no progress gate, and requires_flag: deadline_passed fails lint (not in ENGINE_SET_FLAGS), so the late rows stay visible to on-time players as worse options.
event_voyage_oddity_008.science: Surströmming page, fetched: 'Fermentation continues in the can, causing it to bulge noticeably'; 'In April 2006, several major airlines ... banned the fish, claiming that the pressurised cans of fish are potentially explosive'; producers claim 'it is a myth that the tinned fish can explode'. No claim in the text depends on the cans actually being dangerous.

event_voyage_pair_001.inspired_by: James Lind's 1747 scurvy trial; clinical-trial design played as domestic betrayal.
event_voyage_pair_001.how: The chef and medic have been running a real controlled trial on whether good food heals, and the captain finds out they are the control group, eating dinner ruined to a published standard.
event_voyage_pair_001.science: James Lind page: ship surgeon of HMS Salisbury by 1747; experiment from 20 May 1747 with twelve patients, treatments varied by subgroup, citrus best; 'one of the first reported, controlled, clinical experiments in history'. Fetched with curl, canonical.

event_voyage_pair_002.inspired_by: The engineer who pads every estimate and the pilot who ignores it (Star Trek, Star Wars); bet riff.
event_voyage_pair_002.how: Not at stations, since it needs a live burn. Each has been correcting for the other's safety margin until the gauge carries eleven redlines; a real engine minigame settles the bet, and a perfect run proves both of them wrong. Risk compensation is the idea under the joke.
event_voyage_pair_002.science: Risk compensation page: 'A study of crashes involving taxicabs in Munich of which half had been equipped with anti-lock brakes noted that crash rate was substantially the same for both types of cab, and concluded this was due to drivers of ABS-equipped cabs taking more risks.' MARV's line follows it. Fetched with curl, canonical.

event_voyage_pair_003.inspired_by: Linnaeus and Siegesbeck; the Bone Wars; taxonomic feuds.
event_voyage_pair_003.how: A feud fought by naming the worst organisms aboard after each other, with formal descriptions as insults, and the way out is to offer your own name and let them unite against you.
event_voyage_pair_003.science: Sigesbeckia page: named after Johann Georg Siegesbeck, 'a strong critic' of Linnaeus's classification; 'Linnaeus named a pungent weed Sigesbeckia.' The genus page is live with accepted species, so MARV's 'still in use' holds. Fetched with curl, canonical.

event_voyage_pair_004.inspired_by: State-banquet etiquette; Babette's Feast in reverse; the 1970s miraculin pill.
event_voyage_pair_004.how: The chef learns the diplomat has eaten every dinner on a taste pellet, and the diplomat's reason turns the insult around: the service issues them so an envoy never has a favorite dish, because a preference is leverage. Only 'So was it good?' is left to answer.
event_voyage_pair_004.science: Miraculin page: binds to sweetness receptors; 'normally sour-tasting acidic foods, such as citrus, to be perceived as sweet'; 'The effect can last for one or two hours.' The service's added ingredient is fiction, and the text says so ('declines to itemize'), because real miraculin does not dull other tastes. Fetched with curl, canonical.

event_voyage_pair_005.inspired_by: Space medicine, Spaceflight associated neuro-ocular syndrome; pilots hiding a failing medical; a gentle romance.
event_voyage_pair_005.how: Not at stations, since it needs a live burn. You assume the second seat is a romance and find the medic reading the panel aloud to a pilot who can no longer see it. It is also a romance, and nobody will write that down.
event_voyage_pair_005.science: SANS page (fetched at canonical URL): first case 'reported approximately 3 months after launch when the astronaut noticed that he could now only see Earth clearly while looking through his reading glasses'; globe flattening, hyperopic shifts, loss of near vision, persistent in some. The link posts at event start, so the reveal sits in the opening body and is not spoiled.

event_voyage_pair_006.inspired_by: Two shy people and a shared ticket queue; workplace romance by paperwork.
