event_voyage_pair_006.how: A courtship conducted entirely through false maintenance tickets on a valve that has never stuck, and the captain's choices are to sabotage it, fix it, or roster them together. Fixing it just moves the romance to Valve 4.

event_voyage_pair_007.inspired_by: Specimen or ambassador, a Star Trek staple; Gallup's mirror test.
event_voyage_pair_007.how: A scientist and an envoy agree to settle whether a jar is a person with a mirror test, and it fails by recognizing its reflection as a sovereign power and going to war with it.
event_voyage_pair_007.science: Mirror test page: marked where it 'normally cannot see'; touching the mark is read as recognizing 'its reflection as an image of itself, rather than another animal'; passes listed for great apes, Asian elephant, Eurasian magpie, bluestreak cleaner wrasse; the page says failing 'does not mean they are unable to recognize themselves'. Fetched with curl, canonical.

event_voyage_pair_008.inspired_by: Cold War spy swaps on a bridge; stock versus compost, a real kitchen argument.
event_voyage_pair_008.how: A border goes up over one bucket of peelings, and the feud turns out to be the chef's cover: the botanist has never eaten anything they grew, and the stock was the only way to get any of it into them. Zinnias are excluded by crop_type because a zinnia is not eaten.
event_voyage_pair_008.science: Compost page: 'the microbial oxidation of carbon produces the heat'; 'maintaining high temperatures 130–160 °F (54–71 °C) until the materials are broken down'. Fetched with curl, canonical.

event_voyage_quest_001.inspired_by: Wacky Races, the two claims on one planet in Dune
event_voyage_quest_001.how: Your nemesis hand-delivers your deed, because the Land Office mailed it to the property and the property is their address. Selling here ends the quest early.
event_voyage_quest_001.amended: Batch 4: unless_flag gains bone_on (the fifth quest). Nothing else changed.

event_voyage_quest_002.inspired_by: Wacky Races road signs, Burma-Shave roadside signs
event_voyage_quest_002.how: A rival too scrupulous to falsify a navigation aid: every fake closure carries an asterisk, and even the detour is a pleasant one.

event_voyage_quest_003.inspired_by: Dune's rival claims, The Good, the Bad and the Ugly
event_voyage_quest_003.how: The turn: they ask, badly, with four hundred sleepers behind them, and you can give, refuse, or forge, in rice paper or on the fabricator. The buoy and footnote flags open rows where they answer what you did at step 2.
event_voyage_quest_003.science: Land Rush of 1889 page: people who entered early and hid were identified as Sooners; this led to hundreds of legal contests decided at land offices and by the Department of the Interior.

event_voyage_quest_004.inspired_by: The Good, the Bad and the Ugly's standoff, a landlord sitcom
event_voyage_quest_004.how: One hail, three conversations: blockade for kept or lost (they fold their gun covers), a laughing clerk for the forger, and a lease with clause four for whoever gave. Entry rows are split by requires_flag and hideFlag. The one fight of this quest lives here and records claim_fought with setFlag.

event_voyage_quest_005.inspired_by: Wacky Races finish line, Pheasant Island
event_voyage_quest_005.how: Ending. The nemesis proposes six months each, the deed holder can take the lot and keep four hundred tenants, and whoever gave gets the corner with the spring. Fights and forgeries get a line of memory. Leaving goes to the courts.
event_voyage_quest_005.science: Pheasant Island page: uninhabited river island in the Bidasoa between France and Spain whose administration alternates every six months; a condominium. A note on the page dates the six-month alternation to 1902, so the text says over a hundred years.

event_voyage_quest_006.inspired_by: Pulp Fiction's briefcase, Ronin, The Third Man
event_voyage_quest_006.how: The first lie, and the link exposes it: a heart cannot keep for a trip this long. Lies go: heart, then stolen fortune, then the truth.
event_voyage_quest_006.science: Organ procurement page: historically, hearts and lungs have been transplanted within about six hours of procurement; the time in transport is called cold ischemia time.
event_voyage_quest_006.amended: Batch 4: unless_flag gains bone_on (the fifth quest). Nothing else changed.

event_voyage_quest_007.inspired_by: Pulp Fiction's briefcase, tribute to an idol
event_voyage_quest_007.how: Someone has sent the case a fruit basket. LONG MAY YOU REMAIN SHUT. The chef finds the packing slip (a later answer to the examiner), and the passenger offers a cut (a later trap). A passenger who changes the choices.
event_voyage_quest_007.amended: Batch 4: one row with unless_item locked_case and requires_flag case_on, where the passenger reacts to the jettisoned case (ruling 122). Nothing else changed.

event_voyage_quest_008.inspired_by: Audit of a gold vault, The Third Man
event_voyage_quest_008.how: The turn. A polite examiner with a drill wants to audit the case: the currency of nineteen stations rests on it. Give it, swap in nine kilos of ration brick, or use the slip. The passenger aside is reported speech because layer npcs cannot recall.
event_voyage_quest_008.amended: Batch 4: one row with unless_item locked_case and requires_flag case_on, where the passenger reacts to the jettisoned case (ruling 122). Nothing else changed.

event_voyage_quest_009.inspired_by: Bank runs, the end of Pulp Fiction's what-is-in-the-case question
event_voyage_quest_009.how: Three truths: given, the reserve held one sheet reading ASSETS: SEE CASE and your gold falls; swapped, the currency is now on the Brick Standard because of your lunch; kept or lost, the passenger confesses to flying a central bank. Open it, sink it, or take a cut.

event_voyage_quest_010.inspired_by: Rai stones of Yap, Pulp Fiction
event_voyage_quest_010.how: Kept, given or lost all have an ending, and LOST is the best: the form has three boxes, and a reserve nobody can reach goes on being traded, as the sunk rai stone did. The ledger box works for a player who already jettisoned the case.
event_voyage_quest_010.science: Rai stones page: ownership was established by shared agreement and could be transferred without physical access to the stone; a large rai dropped from a canoe sank to the sea floor, was never seen again, and continued to be transacted as any other stone.

event_voyage_quest_011.inspired_by: Silent Running, real heirloom names such as Mortgage Lifter, the Leningrad seed bank
event_voyage_quest_011.how: A rude seed keeper who openly dislikes you hands over the last of a bean, and the whole quest hangs on one line of a label: do not eat the last ones. Rolled NPC, so the keeper's line is 'keepers', not family.
event_voyage_quest_011.science: Heirloom plant page: 'most authorities agree that heirlooms, by definition, must be open-pollinated'; 'The term heirloom to describe a seed variety was first used in the 1930s ... to describe bean varieties handed down through families.'
event_voyage_quest_011.amended: Batch 4: unless_flag gains bone_on (the fifth quest). Nothing else changed.

event_voyage_quest_012.inspired_by: Wanted posters as a chain letter, seed-bank regeneration
event_voyage_quest_012.how: Word spreads by a bulletin, so the body holds for kept, gave or lost, and only the holder can test the seeds; a test spends the thing it measures. The player's stamp is a small tell.
event_voyage_quest_012.science: Seed bank page: 'seeds eventually degrade with time ... most reputable seed banks monitor germination potential during storage. When seed germination percentage decreases below a prescribed amount, the seeds need to be replanted and fresh seeds collected.'

event_voyage_quest_013.inspired_by: Corporate seed patents; the Name of the Rose's library that keeps a book by making sure nobody reads it
event_voyage_quest_013.how: The turn of the quest, and the antagonist is right: the vault really would keep it alive, forever, ungrown. The decoy leaves Verdance owning, in perpetuity, a small amount of your crop.
event_voyage_quest_013.science: Genetic use restriction technology page: designed to restrict access, 'the seeds sold could not be resown'; 'As of 2025, GURT seeds have not been commercialized anywhere in the world'. MARV's clause about what Verdance sells is fiction built on that.

event_voyage_quest_014.inspired_by: Irish potato famine, Gros Michel, the Leningrad botanists
event_voyage_quest_014.how: Consequence by way of biology: a monoculture bay meets a rust, and the bean is a second plant that stops it. Kept can sow it or eat it, gave has to buy the cure from Verdance, everyone else cuts rows. Soup is the 'lost' ending.
event_voyage_quest_014.science: Crop diversity page: 'if, as in the historic Great Famine of Ireland, a single disease overcomes a variety's resistance, it may destroy an entire harvest, or as in the case of the Gros Michel banana, may cause the commercial extinction of an entire variety.'

event_voyage_quest_015.inspired_by: Leningrad seed bank; every keeper audits the next
event_voyage_quest_015.how: The keeper comes back through npc.recall, nearly out of fuel, to read your line into a ledger. Each ending gets its own entry, and the ugliest one is EATEN. GOOD WITH SALT.
event_voyage_quest_015.science: Institute of Plant Industry page: 28-month siege; 'some 120 tonnes of seeds, nuts and roots'; 'they would rather starve to death than eat the collection. At least 19 of them died, mostly from starvation.'

event_voyage_quest_016.inspired_by: Chain letters, It Follows, medieval book curses
event_voyage_quest_016.how: A stranger pays you to take a library book with kitchen tongs. The debt transfers with the book, fifty-three names so far, and the fine is the only thing on the slip that is still growing.
event_voyage_quest_016.science: Book curse page: 'usually invoking threat of excommunication, or anathema'; 'let him be fried in a pan'; earliest known curse traced to Ashurbanipal's library at Nineveh.
event_voyage_quest_016.amended: Batch 4: unless_flag gains bone_on (the fifth quest). Nothing else changed.

event_voyage_quest_017.inspired_by: 'If you have already returned this item, please disregard this notice'; Brazil's courteous menace
event_voyage_quest_017.how: Every officer is a different rolled face who picks up the last one's sentence mid-word, so the engine's new NPC roll is the joke: the Library's staff are interchangeable and unstoppable. The disregard-this-notice clause also makes the scene true for kept, gave and lost.
event_voyage_quest_017.science: Rule of 72 page: rule number divided by the percentage gives periods to double; 'These rules apply to exponential growth and are therefore used for compound interest as opposed to simple interest'. MARV's figure: 1.02^15600 is about 10^134.2, 135 digits; 72/2 is 36 weeks.

event_voyage_quest_018.inspired_by: Mobile libraries; 'return to any branch' taken literally
event_voyage_quest_018.how: A returns officer sets up a folding table on your airlock and declares themselves a branch. Hand it over, return the ship's manual, or airlock it and have a cadet told to pack.
event_voyage_quest_018.science: List of returned long-overdue library books: Sidney Sussex College book borrowed 1667-68, found 288 years later; record 'largest library book fine paid' $345.14 after 47 years.

event_voyage_quest_019.inspired_by: Ghostbusters' library, Name of the Rose's hidden rulebook, Hitchhiker-style bureaucracy with guns
event_voyage_quest_019.how: The lane's one fight, and it is optional: you may open fire on a library, and the first salvo lands in Comparative Religion. Everyone has a costed way out; the book's holder has the best one, by citing the rule the enforcers have never read.

event_voyage_quest_020.inspired_by: The Name of the Rose (the book is the point), Ankh-Morpork's libraries in spirit only, a comma that cost centuries
event_voyage_quest_020.how: The stranger with the tongs returns by npc.recall in a lanyard. The book is the Library's own rules, signed out to settle an argument about a fine, and the enforcers have been running on memory ever since: they ask you whether they did it right. Keep, gave and gone each get their own ending.

event_voyage_thin_001.inspired_by: Oregon Trail's player-written tombstones, down to the pizza order on the marker.
event_voyage_thin_001.how: A regulation tag gives the wreck its tombstone, passers-by have added to it, and the player's hand goes to the place they really do keep the wrench. The wreck is cut in half so this event and 002 can both fire in one run, on the same lost ship, and each be the half you found.

event_voyage_thin_002.inspired_by: The Oregon Trail grave, plus the bastard machine the batch 2 review asked for: a ship's computer covering itself, with a nod to Brazil's paperwork.
event_voyage_thin_002.how: The wreck's computer blames the dead captain, who is you, and will not open the lockers until an officer signs; its log shows it gave every order both ways and deleted the wrong one. Pencil beats it, and so does the tag from 001, pizza order included.

event_voyage_thin_003.inspired_by: Nothing famous: a real aviation nuisance played as a Far Side premise.
event_voyage_thin_003.how: A fungus eats the fuel, and the big tank and the condenser each solve it the way that thing actually would: settle it or dry it. Non-owners flush, fly on, or let the chef bake it.
event_voyage_thin_003.science: Page: Amorphotheca resinae 'is known to thrive in environments containing alkanes (and water), like aviation fuel, from which it derives its trivial name kerosene fungus', and 'belongs to the heterogenous group of microbial contaminants of diesel fuel'.

event_voyage_thin_004.inspired_by: Mr. Burns blocking out the sun, turned inside out; the real Znamya orbital mirror.
event_voyage_thin_004.how: A bastard machine sells daylight nobody ordered and charges for shade. The insulated bay and the shield each beat it, and everyone else can roll the ship like a chicken, which is the real term of art.
event_voyage_thin_004.science: Spacecraft thermal control page: 'Barbecue roll - a slow roll along the spacecraft's long axis to prevent the Sun over heating one side, like a rotisserie chicken rotating as it is cooked.' MARV's mirror: Znamya (satellite) page, 20 m mirror, 5 km wide bright spot, 1993.

event_voyage_thin_005.inspired_by: Dune's stillsuits and moisture farming, by way of a real desert beetle.
event_voyage_thin_005.how: A surveyor stayed so long studying fog-drinking beetles that they built a leaning post, and the still blueprint is the notebooks' end product. The real choice is plans now or water now.
event_voyage_thin_005.science: Page: 1.4 cm of rain a year; beetle 'stands on a small ridge... Facing into the breeze, with its body angled at 45', droplets gather on bumpy elytra and at about 5 mm roll 'down the beetle's back to its mouthparts'. Southern Africa, per page; the body's world is invented.

event_voyage_thin_006.inspired_by: Doctor Who's weeping angels, with heat in place of blinking; Darwin in the Andes.
event_voyage_thin_006.how: Penitentes point at the sun, the warm hull is a closer sun, and so forty million kneeling ice blades creep toward the ship. Going cold, breaking through, or giving them a better sun are three different ways out.
event_voyage_thin_006.science: Page: 'closely spaced and pointing towards the general direction of the sun'; name 'comes from the resemblance... to a crowd of kneeling people doing penance'; 'a few centimetres to over 5 metres' (Dry Andes); Darwin 'had to squeeze his way through' on March 22, 1835. Blades moving toward a hull is the game's invention.

event_voyage_thin_007.inspired_by: The Star Wars asteroid chase, and every film that has ever shown an asteroid field.
event_voyage_thin_007.how: The real belt is almost empty, so the most frightening stretch on the chart has one garage-sized rock in it and a ship weaving around nothing with great seriousness.
event_voyage_thin_007.science: Page: 'On average the distance between the asteroids is about 965,600 km (600,000 miles)'; 'so thinly distributed that numerous uncrewed spacecraft have traversed it without incident'.

event_voyage_thin_008.inspired_by: The asteroid that turns out to have a mouth (Star Wars), crossed with James Herriot's country vet.
event_voyage_thin_008.how: The cave is a patient, and the person inside is a brisk professional on a house call who needs someone to hold the jaw. The Poultice Blueprint is the fee. A chef does it best, since a poultice is mostly cooking.
event_voyage_thin_008.science: Page: 'Poultices are used on horses to relieve inflammation'; 'They may be used to treat abscesses, with the intention of drawing out pus from the wound'; 'a soft moist mass, often heated and medicated'; 'usually spread on cloth'.

event_voyage_edge_001.inspired_by: Contact (the Machine built from a decoded message, the beach, the eighteen hours of static); the Arecibo message
event_voyage_edge_001.how: A station built the machine from a prime-numbered signal and has been waiting decades for a ship with the right drive, so the player powers, sells, rides or rips out of first contact, and the rider's camera records a day of hold music.
event_voyage_edge_001.science: Wikipedia, Arecibo message: sent once in 1974 toward M13; 'The entire message consisted of 1,679 binary digits'; '1,679 was chosen because it is a semiprime (the product of two prime numbers), to be arranged rectangularly as 73 rows by 23 columns. The alternative arrangement, 23 rows by 73 columns, produces an unintelligible set of characters.' Page opened with curl.

event_voyage_edge_002.inspired_by: Annihilation (the Shimmer copying everything inside it), with the who-is-real dread of The Thing
event_voyage_edge_002.how: The planet has copied your lander three times, perfectly, and one copy is in better repair than yours, so the choices are how much you want to know which one you fly home.

event_voyage_edge_003.inspired_by: Sunshine (the sun as the enemy, the shield angle, the burn on the hull); the YORP effect
event_voyage_edge_003.how: Starlight has spun a whole asteroid field into one giant burning glass whose focus sweeps through the ship's track, so the ship brace-vents through it, eats it with the shield module, EVA-tilts a mirror at the cost of a burn, hides eight days, or burns out.
event_voyage_edge_003.science: Wikipedia, YORP effect: it 'changes the rotation state of a small astronomical body – that is, the body's spin rate and the obliquity of its pole(s) – due to the scattering of solar radiation off its surface and the emission of its own thermal radiation'; 'In 2007, there was direct observational confirmation of the YORP effect on the small asteroids 54509 YORP ... and 1862 Apollo.' Page opened with curl; canonical URL is YORP_effect.

event_voyage_edge_004.inspired_by: Herbig–Haro jets and the protostar's bipolar outflow; star birth played as a delivery, with the medic as midwife
event_voyage_edge_004.how: A star's birth jets pulse across the ship's path at shrinking intervals, and the medic can time them like contractions and keep the ship there to see it through.
event_voyage_edge_004.science: Wikipedia, Herbig–Haro object: 'Some of the accreting material is ejected out along the star's axis of rotation in two jets of partially ionised gas'; HH objects form 'when narrow jets of partially ionised gas ejected by stars collide with nearby clouds of gas and dust at several hundred kilometers per second.' Page opened with curl. The lighting of the core in four days is fiction and no AI line claims it.

event_voyage_edge_005.inspired_by: 2001: A Space Odyssey's last act (the neoclassical room, the older self at dinner, the dropped glass, the shining child above the bed)
event_voyage_edge_005.how: A storage locker becomes a centuries-out-of-date bedroom where an older you is eating dinner and aging by the glance, and the forks are almost right.

event_voyage_edge_006.inspired_by: The Wow! signal and Jerry Ehman's circled printout
event_voyage_edge_006.how: One circled reading has turned a fork lane into a pilgrimage route with a guest book full of NOTHING, and the player can visit, ignore it, or circle something of their own.
event_voyage_edge_006.science: Wikipedia, Wow! signal: detected August 15, 1977 by Ohio State's Big Ear; 'he circled the reading of the signal's intensity, "6EQUJ5", and wrote the comment "Wow!" beside it, leading to the event's widely used name'; 'lasted for the full 72-second window'; 'the signal has never recurred'. 6EQUJ5 is six characters; 'The Wow! signal is essentially confined to one column.' Page opened with curl. The label and text omit the exclamation point on purpose (narrator rule).

event_voyage_edge_007.inspired_by: Event Horizon (the folded paper and the pencil pushed through to explain the gravity drive)
event_voyage_edge_007.how: Someone demonstrated the fold on the real lane and left the pencil in, so the shortcut works and creases every ship, and the choices are squeeze, go round, pull it out, or erase the crease with the other end.

event_voyage_edge_008.inspired_by: The Black Hole (the lit ship hanging at the edge); the textbook picture of a falling object seen from outside
event_voyage_edge_008.how: The first ultra fork: both lanes pass a ship that has been falling into a black hole forever as seen from outside, redder and dimmer, with its call slowed to one note, and every option costs.
event_voyage_edge_008.science: Wikipedia, Event horizon: 'Any object approaching the horizon from the observer's side appears to slow down, never quite crossing the horizon. Due to gravitational redshift, its image reddens over time'; 'A human astronaut would survive the fall through an event horizon only in a black hole with a mass of approximately 10,000 solar masses or greater' (MARV's 'big enough that it went in whole'). Page opened with curl.

event_voyage_identity_014.inspired_by: The botanist card ('Your parents asked what you'd do with that degree. This.'); bedrooms kept as shrines.
event_voyage_identity_014.how: The first thing home has ever asked the botanist is about a houseplant dying of etiolation in their shuttered old room, and the correct diagnosis means telling their parents to stop keeping the room.
event_voyage_identity_014.science: Etiolation page lead: flowering plants grown in partial or complete absence of light; long, weak stems, smaller leaves, pale yellow color; growing tips elongate toward light.

event_voyage_identity_015.inspired_by: The engineer card ('The ship makes sounds it shouldn't. You recognize most of them.'); every mechanic who names their car's noises.
event_voyage_identity_015.how: An engineer who has named every noise aboard hears a new one, a falling bottle-note that turns out to be the water tank singing its own level as it leaks.
event_voyage_identity_015.science: Helmholtz resonance page: blowing across the top of a bottle gives a resonant tone; the cavity volume is in the denominator of the frequency, so a larger volume gives a lower note (cars have a large volume, so wind throb is low).

event_voyage_identity_016.inspired_by: The medic card ('The residency was... there were circumstances.'); the July effect; ward legends told to every new intake.
event_voyage_identity_016.how: The medic's old senior runs this medbay and still tells the intake a cautionary tale about them with a goat in it, three-quarters true, and never says what actually happened.
event_voyage_identity_016.science: July effect page lead: perceived but scientifically unfounded increase in medical errors when US graduates begin residencies; a meta-analysis aggregating over 110 studies found no evidence of a July effect.

event_voyage_identity_017.inspired_by: The xenobiologist card ('You studied aliens. You have never met one.'); peer review; Gary Larson's anthropologists.
event_voyage_identity_017.how: A hive faculty who wrote the definitive thesis on humans without meeting one asks the xenobiologist, who wrote one on hives without meeting one, to choose between two identical jars alone, which their thesis says cannot happen. NPC pinned insect: the joke is the quorum, and a rolled human would have met humans.
event_voyage_identity_017.science: Quorum sensing page, Ants: Temnothorax scouts assess sites, recruit others by tandem running, and once encounter rate at a site passes a threshold (a quorum) the colony moves; no single worker compares all options.

event_voyage_identity_018.inspired_by: REX's setup card ('decommissioned for excessive initiative'); the WWI iron harvest; soldiers who never got word the war was over.
event_voyage_identity_018.how: REX's excessive initiative turns out to be a minefield he laid without orders, still waiting for his voice, and the best way through is letting him tell it the war is over.
event_voyage_identity_018.science: Iron harvest page: annual collection of unexploded ordnance by Belgian and French farmers, mostly found at spring planting and fall plowing, placed at field boundaries for authorities; the French Département du Déminage recovers about 900 tons every year.

event_voyage_identity_019.inspired_by: CHIP's setup card ('CHIP was free with purchase of the ship.'); bundled software; loss leaders.
event_voyage_identity_019.how: CHIP learns it was a free gift with the ship and asks what it is worth; the player can give it a price, a competitor's sponsorship, a reframe, or an unmetered life it cannot stand.
event_voyage_identity_019.science: Loss leader page: a product sold below its minimum profit margin to stimulate other sales; a warehouse chain's hot dog and soda combo at US$1.50, unchanged since 1985 and believed to be well below cost.

event_voyage_identity_020.inspired_by: Obsidian mirrors (the Aztec 'smoking mirror'); long voyages with no mirror aboard.
event_voyage_identity_020.how: A planet of black glass is the first mirror the captain has seen since launch, and the choices are to look, to make the sharpest medkit aboard, or to bring a mirror home for the ship.
event_voyage_identity_020.science: Obsidian page: volcanic glass; used in the eastern Mediterranean for tools and mirrors; Aztec priests used obsidian mirrors; well-crafted obsidian blades can be many times sharper than high-quality steel surgical scalpels, edge about three nanometers.

event_voyage_identity_021.inspired_by: The New England lyrebird that still sang a 1930s flautist's tunes; mimicry as memory.
event_voyage_identity_021.how: A mimic canopy keeps every sound it has heard, including a lost colony's dinner bell and one name called at dusk, and the player can record it, teach it their own name, or answer.
event_voyage_identity_021.science: Lyrebird page: lyrebirds mimic chainsaws, car alarms, camera shutters and more; in 1969 a ranger recorded flute-like song in New England National Park, traced to a 1930s flute player who played tunes near his pet lyrebird, which kept them after release into the park.

event_voyage_identity_022.inspired_by: The SOFAR channel and its downed-pilot distress charges; memorial roll calls.
event_voyage_identity_022.how: A dead raft colony's buoy still reads its roll call into the deep sound channel each dawn on a dying cell that fits your ship, so keeping the memory alive is paid in fuel.
event_voyage_identity_022.science: SOFAR channel page: a horizontal layer of minimum sound speed acting as a waveguide; low-frequency sound may travel thousands of miles; in WWII the US Navy developed locating the explosion of a SOFAR bomb used as a distress signal by downed pilots.

event_voyage_quest_021.inspired_by: Earth's museums emptying onto colony ships; the Lovecraft expedition fossils that were not quite fossils; Alien's fossilized pilot; Quatermass and the Pit
event_voyage_quest_021.how: Every ship leaving a dying Earth takes one exhibit, and you draw the drawer at the back: a set of seventeen pieces whose deed of gift forbids any two on one ship, withdrawn from display because visitors would not leave it. Grants the unidentified bone that event_station_027 and event_shipboard_024 need, and matches their account: a mineral cast, warm, a place people like to sit.
event_voyage_quest_021.science: Fossil page, Casts and molds: "In some cases, the original remains of the organism completely dissolve or are otherwise destroyed. The remaining organism-shaped hole in the rock is called an external mold. If this void is later filled with sediment, the resulting cast resembles what the organism looked like."

event_voyage_quest_022.inspired_by: The Shining's ballroom crowd, ghost ships in convoy, Quatermass and the Pit
event_voyage_quest_022.how: Piece nine's ship has flown your heading for three days and wants nothing, only to see; its whole crew sits in the warm common room facing the crate. Kept players can show the join (and the crate turns toward its match in the night); lost players get an unless_item row and watch the ship go back to look for it.

event_voyage_quest_023.inspired_by: Alien's space jockey, the scattered pieces of a cursed relic, a deed of gift that anticipated its own author
event_voyage_quest_023.how: The turn: the curator who split the set has gathered sixteen pieces and asks, nicely, for yours, though the deed they wrote forbids it "including the curator". Give it for the upkeep fund, refuse, or send a strut from your cargo frame in museum cloth (costs hull). The bone_matched row shows that Nine is now in the curator's hold.

event_voyage_quest_024.inspired_by: Event Horizon's open airlock, the Mary Celeste, Annihilation, The Shining
event_voyage_quest_024.how: The tender sits dark across the lane with its airlock open and its beacon reading the opening hours. Inside, the sitters ring the frame: whole if you gave, whole around your strut if you tricked, a space at one end if you kept or lost it. Sitting down "for a minute" costs eight days; lost players can take one of theirs (unless_item) and kept players can still lay theirs in the space.

event_voyage_quest_025.inspired_by: Museum deaccession paperwork, The Shining's last photograph, the end of a ghost story told by the ghost
event_voyage_quest_025.how: The curator is up again, writing the statement of justification for removing the thing from the collection, with the object's name left blank. Gave: take a piece they sawed off, or leave it whole with its sitters. Tricked: take your strut back, warmer than the rest, or admit the real piece never left your hold ("Then what have we all been sitting with?"). Kept: keep it apart, or give it now. Lost: "location: somewhere", the best outcome the museum could hope for.
event_voyage_quest_025.science: Deaccessioning page: "Deaccessioning is the process by which a work of art or other object is permanently removed from a museum's collection to sell it or otherwise dispose of it"; "The process begins with the curator creating a document called a \"statement of justification\"".

event_species_human_005.inspired_by: Nature documentaries in hushed voices; the Hawthorne effect; time-lapse filming.
event_species_human_005.how: A rock naturalist cannot film a natural human because every human it films stops being natural, and at rock speed humans only come out sharp when standing in a queue.
event_species_human_005.science: Hawthorne effect page: individuals modify their behavior in response to awareness of being observed; studies 1924 to 1932 at the Hawthorne Works, a Western Electric factory; some scholars think the descriptions are fictitious. MARV's line: light was raised and then lowered in the experiment room, and productivity rose in both rooms each time (illumination experiment 1924 to 1927).

event_species_human_006.inspired_by: Biosphere 2's first closure (factions, falling oxygen, the concrete); every neighbor dispute.
event_species_human_006.how: Two botanists twenty meters apart in a sealed dome blame each other for the falling air: hand them their own notes and they agree with themselves while still suffocating, or prove the concrete did it and they find a new feud.
event_species_human_006.science: Biosphere 2 page: 3.14 acres, Oracle, Arizona; first mission 1991 to 1993, four women and four men; before it was half over the group had split into two factions barely on speaking terms. Also on the page, used only in the reveal (not the link): oxygen 20.9% to 14.5% in 16 months, about 4,080 m; carbon dioxide reacted with exposed concrete to form calcium carbonate, sequestering carbon and oxygen; concrete sealed before the second mission.

event_species_human_007.inspired_by: Castaway-made-king stories; honey bee swarms following the queen; decision fatigue.
event_species_human_007.how: A hive that decides everything by quorum crowned the first human who ever said 'left' without a vote, and the way out is to give it something else that decides alone: a coin. after_progress 0.5 keeps the hive out of human space on every trail.
event_species_human_007.science: Quorum sensing page, Social insects: Temnothorax ants and honey bees choose new nest sites by quorum; once a quorum is sensed the colony moves; 'no single worker may have visited and compared all of the available options'. MARV's swarm line: in swarming the queen leaves the hive with a portion of the workers.

event_species_water_009.inspired_by: Weddings at sea; 'in sickness and in health'; the triple point as a physical vow.
event_species_water_009.how: Water people marry only at the triple point, where each partner is ice, water and steam at once, so the player must hold an airlock at 611 pascals for the vows, and hurrying them leaves the steam unmarried. Every wedding path but the hurried one sets water_sampled, a second way into The Reply.
event_species_water_009.science: Triple point page: water 273.16 K, 0.01 °C, vapour pressure 611.657 Pa (0.00603659 atm, so about 1/166 atm as MARV says); the unique combination where liquid water, ice and vapour coexist in stable equilibrium. MARV's chapel line follows the phase diagram: above that pressure vapour condenses, below it liquid boils off.

event_species_reptile_009.inspired_by: Diogenes asking Alexander to stand out of his sun; basking lizards; a tuatara's third eye.
event_species_reptile_009.how: Your ship's shadow tells a basking elder's third eye that night has fallen, so it closes the day's accounts; lifting off spreads the early night down the whole beach in order of age and sets reptile_warrant_out, a second way to the bounty hunter.
event_species_reptile_009.science: Parietal eye page: photoreceptive, at the top of the head, associated with the pineal gland, which regulates circadian rhythmicity and hormone production for thermoregulation; found in the tuatara and most lizards.

event_voyage_station_001.inspired_by: The Grand Budapest Hotel (the concierges' secret society and its phone-chain montage)
event_voyage_station_001.how: The concierges' secret society becomes station janitors who know each other by a mop wring and pass favors down the lane by hand, so the price of a free repair is holding someone's mop while the call goes by, and a wrong wring gets you mourned.

event_voyage_station_002.inspired_by: Cheers (the regulars greeted by name, the know-it-all postman)
event_voyage_station_002.how: The dockmaster's office is run like a neighborhood bar for ships, and the regulars have bet for nine years on whether a stranger will ever correct the pilot who says the far side of the Moon is dark.
event_voyage_station_002.science: Far side of the Moon page: 'dark' means unseen, not unlit; each location on the Moon gets two weeks of sunlight; the far side (82% of it) went unobserved until Luna 3 photographed it in 1959.

event_voyage_station_003.inspired_by: Star Trek: Deep Space Nine (the promenade's tailor everyone knows is a spy, and his contradictory life stories)
event_voyage_station_003.how: The spy who insists he is only a tailor becomes a promenade botanist whom security watches by buying a fern every morning, and what the most dangerous person on the ring hands you is a fungus that later turns into cheese.

event_voyage_station_004.inspired_by: Casablanca (the man who came for the waters, in a desert)
event_voyage_station_004.how: A spa medbay famous for its healing spring, which was sold off by the block before the plaque was cast; the medic runs the cure in the patients' own water and quietly does real medicine under cover of the bath.
event_voyage_station_004.science: Balneotherapy page: treating disease by bathing, usually at spas, used since ancient times; a 2009 review of all published clinical evidence found the research not strong enough to draw firm conclusions about its efficacy.

event_voyage_station_005.inspired_by: Casablanca (the letters of transit nobody can rescind, the refugees waiting for them, and the order to arrest the usual crowd)
event_voyage_station_005.how: Two departure letters that no living authority can revoke turn up in your galley during a ring-wide lockdown, and you decide who gets to stop waiting: the police, the ship that has waited longest, the highest bidder, or nobody.

event_voyage_station_006.inspired_by: The Grand Budapest Hotel (a faded grand hotel whose staff keep its standards to the end, and its lobby boy)
event_voyage_station_006.how: A once-grand station's four hundred staff insist on valeting your ship with eighty-year-old machinery that removes hull patches as unsightly, and the hard part is refusing hospitality without breaking anyone's heart.

event_voyage_trail_001.inspired_by: Apollo 8's Earthrise and the commander's joke that the picture wasn't scheduled; commuters who have stopped looking.
event_voyage_trail_001.how: The ship's flight plan, like Apollo 8's, has no line for the view, and the one choice the plan would make costs you the sight of a dying Earth looking fine.
event_voyage_trail_001.science: Earthrise page: taken December 24, 1968 on Apollo 8, the first crewed voyage to orbit the Moon; the crew 'became the first humans to witness an Earthrise'; Borman (joking) 'it's not scheduled'; Anders asked Lovell for a roll of color film. No quote reproduced; the body paraphrases. MARV's ninety-second window and the shuttle are fiction.

event_voyage_trail_002.inspired_by: Apollo astronauts' reports that Moon dust smelled of spent gunpowder; the sample bottles whose seals it ruined.
event_voyage_trail_002.how: The Moon follows the crew indoors and has to be got out again, with a magnet because it is partly iron.
event_voyage_trail_002.science: Lunar regolith page (Lunar_soil redirects here, so the canonical URL is used): 'sharp and very adhesive particles, with a distinct gunpowder taste and smell'; 'tastes and smells of spent gunpowder'; grit deteriorated the knife-edge indium seals of Apollo sample bottles and air leaked in; agglutinates carry tiny specks of elemental iron, and vacuuming suits with a magnet is a listed mitigation (hence 'much of it', not 'every grain'); thale cress grown in regolith in 2022 (the botanist's 'plants have grown in it').

event_voyage_trail_003.inspired_by: Proposals for far-side radio telescopes shielded from Earth; the National Radio Quiet Zone idea, pushed to a buoy that asks every ship to switch off.
event_voyage_trail_003.how: The quietest place near home asks for two days of silence, and the cheapest way through is to be the only thing the dish ever recorded.
event_voyage_trail_003.science: Far side of the Moon page: 'Because the far side of the Moon is shielded from radio transmissions from the Earth, it is considered a good location for placing radio telescopes'; 'the area around the telescopes must be protected against contamination by other radio sources'. The dish, buoy and noisy lamp drivers are fiction.

event_voyage_trail_004.inspired_by: Kessler syndrome as a daily forecast; the ISS's one-in-10,000 rule and its crew sheltering in the Soyuz; the Shuttle flying tail-first; the STS-7 paint fleck.
event_voyage_trail_004.how: Near home the debris is weather now, and every way through it is a real one spacecraft have used, each costing something different.
event_voyage_trail_004.science: Space debris page: ISS maneuvers if 'there is a greater than a one-in-10,000 chance of a debris strike'; management 'asked the crew to shelter in the Soyuz on three occasions due to late debris-proximity warnings'; the Shuttle 'was later flown tail-first to take a greater proportion of the debris load on the engines and rear cargo bay'; on STS-7 a fleck of paint pitted the front window 'over 1 mm' wide; Kessler (2010) says a cascade may not be obvious until well advanced. MARV: 1 - (299/300)^12 = 0.039, about one in 25.5.

event_voyage_trail_005.inspired_by: Colony politics arriving months stale (brief seed); Brazil's paperwork; absentee ballots.
event_voyage_trail_005.how: Light takes minutes but the free news tier takes months, so the player can join an election that ended, and a late vote is kept for the next one.

event_voyage_trail_006.inspired_by: Radio delay as two monologues (brief seed); recorded phone menus.
event_voyage_trail_006.how: The landing office has stopped conversing and now speaks in complete branching speeches, and each way of answering it costs something different.
event_voyage_trail_006.science: Speed of light page: 'if a robot on the surface of Mars were to encounter a problem, its human controllers would not be aware of it until approximately 4–24 minutes later. It would then take a further 4–24 minutes for commands to travel from Earth to Mars.' The same paragraph also gives 'five and twenty minutes'; the link uses the 4–24 figure. The ship's nine minutes each way is fiction for a mid-route position.

event_voyage_trail_007.inspired_by: Phobos's tiny gravity; baggage handlers; the brief's Phobos seed.
event_voyage_trail_007.how: On a moon you can throw things off, the new dockhand does, and the player chooses how to get two crates back out of orbit.
event_voyage_trail_007.science: Phobos (moon) page: escape velocity 11.39 m/s (41 km/h); orbits Mars in 7 hours 39 minutes, faster than Mars rotates; 'closer to its primary body than any other known natural satellite to a planet'; dimensions about 26 × 23 × 18 km; 'may be a rubble pile'. The page has a feature whose name the checker bans, and it is not used.

event_voyage_trail_008.inspired_by: Juno's dust hits suggesting Mars as the source of zodiacal dust; the brief's dust seed, kept in flight because Storm Season already has the landing.
event_voyage_trail_008.how: The long middle of the Mars run is dusty with Mars itself, and the dust comes from behind, so the right move is to turn the ship round.
event_voyage_trail_008.science: Juno (spacecraft) page: 'In 2021, analysis of the frequency of interplanetary dust impacts (primarily on the backs of the solar panels), as Juno passed between Earth and the asteroid belt, indicated that this dust, which causes the zodiacal light, comes from Mars'. The Zodiacal light page says other dust instruments found no sign of a Mars source, so the link says 'suggested'. Hits on the stern and a thick dust lane are fiction drawn from it.

event_voyage_trigger_001.inspired_by: Baseball's no-hitter superstition: nobody in the dugout mentions it.
event_voyage_trigger_001.how: The crew will not jinx a thriving crop by saying so, and touch it for luck instead, which is the one thing that really does slow a plant down; breaking the jinx is what saves the streak.
event_voyage_trigger_001.science: Wikipedia, Thigmomorphogenesis: plants alter growth in response to touch, wind or rain; 'repeated mechanical stimulation suppresses internode elongation and promotes radial stem growth, resulting in shorter, sturdier plants', and greenhouse plants are taller and more slender than stockier outdoor ones. Page opened with curl.

event_voyage_trigger_002.inspired_by: Golden Age pirate articles; Treasure Island's crew eyeing the chest.
event_voyage_trigger_002.how: A rich ship's crew drafts real pirate articles (two shares for the captain, a limb fund, an oath on the fire axe) and pins them to the captain's door, so the gold becomes a constitutional question rather than a robbery.
event_voyage_trigger_002.science: Wikipedia, Pirate code (history, not science): crews drafted and swore to written articles before a voyage, sometimes on a hatchet for want of a Bible; Bartholomew Roberts' articles gave captain and quartermaster two shares each and ordinary crewmen one, and paid 800 pieces of eight from the common fund to any man who lost a limb; a captain could be deposed by majority vote; articles were often posted on the captain's cabin door. Page opened with curl.

event_voyage_trigger_003.inspired_by: The bootstrapping problem; RepRap; Brazil's part numbers.
event_voyage_trigger_003.how: The only machine that can make the missing gear is the one missing it, so the player chooses which other system to rob for a few days (water or dinner), files one by hand, or has the engineer coax one last print for a full repair.
event_voyage_trigger_003.science: Wikipedia, RepRap: 'a project to develop low-cost 3D printers that can print most of their own components', started in 2005 at the University of Bath. Page opened with curl.

event_voyage_trigger_004.inspired_by: Photocopies of photocopies; Multiplicity's degrading clones.
event_voyage_trigger_004.how: A worn fabricator prints each job from the last print instead of the file, so every cup is vaguer than the one before; the player can service it, find the first cup to copy from, or run the decay to its end for scrap.
event_voyage_trigger_004.science: Wikipedia, Generation loss: 'the loss of quality between subsequent copies'; in analog audio and video editing it was a major consideration, careful planning was required to minimize it, and noise is a main cause. Page opened with curl.

event_voyage_trigger_005.inspired_by: Hospital price lists, and the real medical leech-and-maggot cabinet.
event_voyage_trigger_005.how: The cheap cure at the pharmacy counter is a teabag of sterile maggots, and it works; the player weighs gold, water, days and squeamishness against flying on. Patient may be the captain: every line uses {patient.name}, no crew-only wording, no medic gate (the medic may be the patient). The fly-on outcome leaves the death or the engine's save line to the engine.
event_voyage_trigger_005.science: Wikipedia, Maggot therapy: live, disinfected maggots introduced into wounds to clean out necrotic tissue; in 2003 the US FDA cleared green bottle fly maggots as a 'medical device'; they can debride a wound in a day or two and grow from about 2 mm to about 10 mm in 48 to 72 hours; patients report a tickling sensation; a Cochrane review found it broadly as effective as most other debridement methods. Page opened with curl.

event_voyage_trigger_006.inspired_by: Cruise-ship muster drills; the extra kid in the class photo.
event_voyage_trigger_006.how: The stowaway is not caught but counted: a lifeboat drill comes up one head over, and the extra person is the only one wearing the suit correctly. Welcome rows leave `sub` empty so the engine's join note shows; every row sets stowaway_resolve.

event_voyage_trigger_007.how: The laid-up crewmate turns the navigation scope on a freighter sharing the lane and builds a murder case in the margins of a medical leaflet; the player can hail, chase the jettisoned crate (rations and one boot), make them rest, or make them a real lookout. It is never solved.

event_voyage_trigger_008.inspired_by: Kitchen-scrap gardening; The Martian's potatoes; Silent Running's last dome.
event_voyage_trigger_008.how: With the crop dead, the bay is a garden with nothing in it: plant the pantry's beans and sprouting potatoes, drain the reservoir for water, or bag the still-living soil for the colony. Grim and gentle; nothing revives the crop.
event_voyage_trigger_008.science: Wikipedia, Soil biology: bacteria 'with populations ranging from 100 million to 3 billion in a teaspoon of productive soil'. Page opened with curl.

event_voyage_trigger_009.inspired_by: Turbine blade creep; a car pulling to one side; Douglas Adams' autopilot that does not mention things.
event_voyage_trigger_009.how: Too long at PLAID and the hot drive mounts have sagged, so the thrust is off-center and the ship has been flying a slow circle the autopilot quietly paid for in fuel; the fixes trade fuel, days, a bulkhead, or moving the middle of the ship.
event_voyage_trigger_009.science: Wikipedia, Creep (deformation): slow permanent deformation under persistent stress, 'more severe in materials that are subjected to heat for long periods'; 'creep of a turbine blade could cause the blade to contact the casing'. Page opened with curl.

event_voyage_quest_026.inspired_by: Brazil's ministries; Hitchhiker's planning notices left in a basement for years; the diplomatic letter that needs a name to address it to.
event_voyage_quest_026.how: Earth asked a hive one question for a treaty, who signs for you, and the reply can only be collected in person by whoever holds Earth's place in its queue, and a place in a hive queue is a smell in a jar.
event_voyage_quest_026.science: Wikipedia, Chemical communication in insects: chemical signals serve to mark a trail, recognize nest-mates and mark territory, among other functions; the use of scents is especially well developed in social insects.

event_voyage_quest_027.inspired_by: Legislative riders; the human queue mirroring the hive's.
event_voyage_quest_027.how: Humans, the species that invented forms, queue up at the lock to add their own drops to Earth's question: a mining concern pays for a clause, a school adds what are your names, and both come back at the end.

event_voyage_quest_028.inspired_by: Letting someone go ahead of you in line, taken to its limit; Oregon Trail's hard trade-offs.
event_voyage_quest_028.how: A queenless tender of nurses with a brood days from chilling asks for Earth's place; you can hand over the jar, keep it with perfect hive manners, or mix their smell into Earth's so the jar carries one joint motion, because a document here is something you wear.
event_voyage_quest_028.science: Wikipedia, Eusociality: defined by cooperative brood care, overlapping generations within a colony, and division of labor into reproductive and non-reproductive groups; individuals of at least one caste usually lose the ability to do what another caste does.

event_voyage_quest_029.inspired_by: Event 006's queue-as-government; inaugurations; the hive's one-motion head of state.
event_voyage_quest_029.how: Reaching the front makes whoever wears Earth's smell head of state, with one motion and a filing past of six billion that builds a comb on the bow by stigmergy; kept, shared and gave each play their own layer, and the Hive Lozenge makes the ship a wing so everything carries at once.
event_voyage_quest_029.science: Wikipedia, Stigmergy: indirect coordination through the environment in which a trace left by one action stimulates the next action; termites build pillars, arches and chambers by dropping pheromone-laced mud where nestmates have already dropped it.

event_voyage_quest_030.inspired_by: Hitchhiker's answers that are worse than the question; the form with one empty box.
event_voyage_quest_030.how: The quorum answers NAME OF RESPONSIBLE PARTY with WHOEVER ASKED, so Earth is now in charge of six billion insects and the player chooses whose name goes in the box; the unasked paths end with the ministry starting again from the back, or a brood the player saved carrying the question for generations.

event_voyage_quest_041.inspired_by: Hitchhiker's planning-office notices filed somewhere nobody looks; Brazil's endless correspondence; every centuries-long lawsuit in fiction.
event_voyage_quest_041.how: Humanity is legally a child in reptile space because nobody human has ever turned two hundred, and Earth's petition to be treated as grown up has finally come up for hearing after one hundred and ninety years; any human may appear, so you do.
event_voyage_quest_041.science: Age of majority: the age at which the law treats a person as an adult, in control of their own actions and decisions; most countries set it at 18 (Wikipedia, Age of majority).

event_voyage_quest_042.inspired_by: Lobbyists against any reform that would make them accountable; Peter Pan as a trade association.
event_voyage_quest_042.how: The human traders who work reptile space have built forty years of business on being children who cannot be sued, and they will pay you to lose the docket, tell you why the reptiles keep humans young, or take their money back.

event_voyage_quest_043.inspired_by: Bleak House's Chancery; The Merchant of Venice's price read out before judgment; the way kind institutions keep people dependent.
event_voyage_quest_043.how: The reptile bench will grant majority but reads you the price first: two centuries of heat no one could bill a minor for falls due, and humans, unable to shed, would carry it forever, so the court kindly asks you to withdraw, and you can press, withdraw, or amend so a generation counts as a skin.
event_voyage_quest_043.science: Moulting: a snake sheds by rubbing against something hard until the skin splits, then crawls out; the skin often comes away in one piece, turned inside out. Lizards also consume their shed skin (used in step 4's laid_down outcome, no separate link).

event_voyage_quest_044.inspired_by: Court orders served by process servers who never give up; Kafka; a guardian ad litem taken entirely literally.
event_voyage_quest_044.how: The ruling is served by the usher after the eldest seals it on its way into brumation, and each verdict bites differently: an adult human is billed the first installment, a minor must tow its brumating judge-guardian and keep it watered, and an amending species must demonstrate a shed, which a captain does by resigning and succeeding themself.
event_voyage_quest_044.science: Dormancy, Brumation section: ectotherms such as lizards go dormant in the cold in a way different from hibernation, called brumation, and periodic water intake is required.

event_voyage_quest_045.inspired_by: Coming-of-age ceremonies; the rule that only certain ranks may speak to certain others; Wodehouse butlers addressing the wall.
event_voyage_quest_045.how: The usher turned two hundred during the voyage, so it may now speak only to adults: if humanity grew up, it says your name, the first time a reptile has said a human's to the human, and if humanity stayed young, it reads the order to the bulkhead beside you, kindly.

event_voyage_quest_046.inspired_by: Standing orders and auto-renewals; product succession and end of support; the last shift at a closing plant.
event_voyage_quest_046.how: Earth's last robot plant closes after building one unit to a four-hundred-year-old standing order from robot space, and its last shift wheels the crate into your airlock in person.

event_voyage_quest_047.inspired_by: Bit rot on stored media; a supplier apologizing by letter after the fact.
event_voyage_quest_047.how: Among humans, the plant writes from somebody's kitchen to say the crate has the wrong standby cell, so the player chooses between fuel, gold or letting the unit's memory fade, which matters later.
event_voyage_quest_047.science: Data degradation (Wikipedia): the gradual corruption of computer data from an accumulation of non-critical failures, also called bit rot; flash memory and EPROMs store data as electrical charges that can slowly leak away through imperfect insulation.

event_voyage_quest_048.inspired_by: End-of-support notices; manuals nobody finishes; the successor that obsoletes its predecessor.
event_voyage_quest_048.how: Robot space reads its manual's last page for the first time and finds that support for its whole line ends when the next model first powers on, so it asks you not to complete the delivery it ordered.

event_voyage_quest_049.inspired_by: Cosmic-ray bit flips; the accidental launch drill; shielding a signal with water.
event_voyage_quest_049.how: A single particle flips the bit that meant not yet, the next model starts its first power-on wherever it is, and each earlier choice decides what you can do about its announcement: muffle it in water, pull its cell, or let it speak.
event_voyage_quest_049.science: Single-event upset (Wikipedia): a change of state caused by one single ionizing particle striking a sensitive node in a live micro-electronic device such as a memory bit; the error is a soft error and not considered permanently damaging.

event_voyage_quest_050.inspired_by: Closing a purchase order; auto-renewal to a defunct supplier; backward compatibility as an act of kindness.
event_voyage_quest_050.how: Robot space's procurement closes the order and renews it automatically to Earth's closed plant, and the courier states how the delivery went, from a quiet colonist to a newborn patching itself to support the line it ended.
event_voyage_quest_050.science: Backward compatibility (Wikipedia): a property of an operating system, software or product that allows interoperability with an older legacy system or input designed for it; breaking it usually incurs costs.

event_voyage_quest_031.inspired_by: Hitchhiker's planning-office indifference, played from the other side; the Ordnance Survey benchmarks cut into old stone.
event_voyage_quest_031.how: Humanity's forty-one apologies to a rock elder are all in the rock almanac as weather, so a one-officer Rock Desk hands you the forty-second and a grain of Earth's oldest zircon to swear it on, because rocks only hear promises vouched for by something older than the grudge.
event_voyage_quest_031.science: Zircons from the Jack Hills, Western Australia, have U–Pb ages up to 4.404 billion years, the oldest minerals yet dated on Earth (Wikipedia: Zircon).

event_voyage_quest_032.inspired_by: Brazil's paperwork, and every treaty drafted by the side that started the war.
event_voyage_quest_032.how: The survey firm that cut the benchmark (and staked a quarry claim the same day) offers to pay for three words on the end of humanity's apology, Except under license, or to buy the witness outright, since without it the rocks will file the promise as harmless weather.
event_voyage_quest_032.science: A benchmark was originally a level line chiseled into stone so a leveling rod could be repositioned in exactly the same place; bronze or aluminum disks set in stone are now common (Wikipedia: Benchmark (surveying)).

event_voyage_quest_033.inspired_by: Zardoz's stone head and the Ents' hasty meeting, pushed to an elder who has nearly reached the verb of a two-century reply.
event_voyage_quest_033.how: The turn: the elder will hear the oath only if it is read at her speed and sworn on something that lasts, and she would like the zircon, which to her is a very small grandmother, to stay with her; give it, keep it (a second grievance), swear on the Slow Writ in an afternoon, or swear on your word and be politely filed as drizzle.

event_voyage_quest_034.inspired_by: Mining-company westerns and Avatar's unobtainium, made quiet: the victim will not notice for a century.
event_voyage_quest_034.how: The firm is coring the elder under its claim, and she will remember whoever was standing by when she finally notices; block the drill with your hull, hold the zircon to her face (rocks hurry for an elder), refund the fee if you took it, read the promise until they give a promise of their own, or take a share.

event_voyage_quest_035.inspired_by: Oregon Trail's tombstone record and a farmer's almanac, kept on a ten-thousand-year schedule.
event_voyage_quest_035.how: The keeper of the rock almanac writes humanity's entry for the next ten thousand years from what you did: climate (with the zircon left as witness or kept for the new world), a weather that held with no word for it yet, a fault with your ship's name twice, late climate, or drizzle as always.
event_voyage_quest_035.science: Deep time is geological time spanning billions of years, beyond human experience; the concept was developed by James Hutton in the 18th century, and Earth is dated at around 4.55 billion years (Wikipedia: Deep time).

event_voyage_quest_051.inspired_by: The old joke about the statistician who drowned crossing a river of average depth one meter; Brazil's paperwork; marine insurance.
event_voyage_quest_051.how: An Earth insurer calls because the unknown reinsurer has already paid out on your ship's total loss, at the route's average: thirty-one percent of a total loss, which is not a thing that can happen to anybody.

event_voyage_quest_052.inspired_by: Marine salvage and subrogation played straight; Far Side premise of the polite tradesman with the wrong job.
event_voyage_quest_052.how: Because the loss was paid, a human salvage tug has bought the rights to thirty-one percent of your wreck and shows up to cut along the dotted lines of the average wreck, while you are still flying it.
event_voyage_quest_052.science: Total loss page: in a total loss the insurer indemnifies the assured in full and ownership passes to the insurer (subrogation); a total loss may be presumed when a ship disappears and no news is received within a reasonable time.

event_voyage_quest_053.inspired_by: Hitchhiker's improbability as a legal defense; Boltzmann brains; an insurance assessor who arrives to inspect a wreck that is still talking.
event_voyage_quest_053.how: The unknown reinsurer comes to help you be lost the right amount, and the turn is how you balance its book: hand back the claim, let it collect, argue that you are a statistical fluctuation, or show it a receipt for a paid account.
event_voyage_quest_053.science: Boltzmann brain page: the thought experiment suggests a brain with false memories is more probable to form spontaneously by random fluctuation than the universe forming the way cosmologists think; Sean Carroll noted it works at larger scales, like entire bodies or even galaxies.

event_voyage_quest_054.inspired_by: Final Destination's schedule of accidents, recast as an installment plan; Oregon Trail's breakdowns.
event_voyage_quest_054.how: The loss is collected in the ordinary way: parts fail on the hour, at thirty-one percent, and the way through depends on what you did with the claim (work ahead of its schedule, pay evenly on account, buy cover late, stay improbable, or be already paid).

event_voyage_quest_055.inspired_by: The Drake equation used as an actuarial table; closing an insurance file.
event_voyage_quest_055.how: The assessor closes your file with a chain of guessed factors that multiplies out to exactly one, then settles up according to whether you kept, returned, lost or argued your way out of the claim.
event_voyage_quest_055.science: Drake equation page: formulated in 1961 by Frank Drake as a probabilistic argument multiplying factors to estimate the number of communicative civilizations in the Milky Way; criticism notes several factors are so conjectural the equation cannot draw firm conclusions.

event_voyage_quest_036.inspired_by: The decennial census and the enumerator's knock; Brazil's form-first bureaucracy; Hitchhiker's flat treatment of planet-sized paperwork.
event_voyage_quest_036.how: A tired human census clerk deputizes your ship to count a population that merges and parts at will, with a one-question form, and admits that whatever isn't counted as someone gets licensed as volume.

event_voyage_quest_037.inspired_by: Water-rights speculators and company towns; the fox bidding on the henhouse.
event_voyage_quest_037.how: A volume firm offers to buy the blank return or hand you free ice, and the ice turns out to have been cut from a pond that was arguing with itself.

event_voyage_quest_038.inspired_by: Census-day household forms; the merged clerk-assessor of event_species_water_003; coalescing droplets.
event_voyage_quest_038.how: Nine water people merged into one to survive a drought and ask to be counted as ONE, knowing the rest of them then becomes harvestable volume; the turn is honesty against survival, and anyone who took the ice finds their drinking tank holds the household's missing tenth.
event_voyage_quest_038.science: Coalescence is the process by which two or more droplets merge during contact to form a single daughter droplet; in clouds, colliding droplets coalesce until they are large enough to fall as rain (Wikipedia, Coalescence (physics)).

event_voyage_quest_039.inspired_by: Prior-appropriation water law and the Western water wars; repossession men; Oregon Trail flatness about loss.
event_voyage_quest_039.how: A licensed harvesting rig works from the census map, so whatever you wrote decides what it cuts: a surplus, an unnamed tenth from a parting, a person sold as ice, or your own uncounted tank.
event_voyage_quest_039.science: Prior appropriation gives the first person to take a quantity of water for beneficial use the right to keep using it, summarized 'first in time, first in right'; the right can be abrogated if not used for an extended period (Wikipedia, Prior-appropriation water rights).

event_voyage_quest_040.inspired_by: The census's last box for the head of household; water's view (from event_species_water_001) that a crew sharing one reclaimed tank is already one conversation.
event_voyage_quest_040.how: The return comes due, and the water people point out that by their reckoning a ship whose crew all drink the same recycled tank is a household of one.
event_voyage_quest_040.science: Census enumerations must determine which individuals can be counted; every person should be identified uniquely as a resident in one place, which matters for people with multiple or temporary addresses (Wikipedia, Census).
